specificity.statement: the Bill has already breached te Tiriti o Waitangi in its policy development, and has completely ignored the significant opposition and feedback provided in over 22,000 submissions.
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete submission count but the 'breach' claim is asserted, not detailed.

civility.statement: This Bill is the same tired politics we have seen time and time again from the Government, attacking Te Tiriti o Waitangi to make it easier for wealthy companies to exploit our whānau and our taiao for profit.
civility.explanation: Harsh characterisation of Government motives rather than the Bill's provisions.

veracity.statement: the Bill has already breached te Tiriti o Waitangi in its policy development, and has completely ignored the significant opposition and feedback provided in over 22,000 submissions.
veracity.explanation: Submission volume is a checkable figure; 'breached te Tiriti' and 'completely ignored' are contestable characterisations.

rigor.statement: This Bill is the same tired politics we have seen time and time again from the Government, attacking Te Tiriti o Waitangi to make it easier for wealthy companies to exploit our whānau and our taiao for profit.
rigor.explanation: Imputes motive ('to make it easier for wealthy companies to exploit') without evidence linking the Bill to that outcome.

civility.statement: Today a majority of powerful people prioritised cynical politics, fanning the flame of a culture war, over the truth and the needs of our nation,
civility.explanation: Attributes bad motives ('cynical politics') to opponents rather than debating the policy.

civility.statement: You are what you do, and today Government MPs showed us who they are. When you wear the mask for a while, it becomes your face.
civility.explanation: Character-based jibe ('the mask... becomes your face') aimed at opponents rather than their arguments.

veracity.statement: The Prime Minister has told us that there’s nothing that he likes about this Bill, calling it ‘divisive’ himself. He has told us the National Party do not support this Bill, as did every other National MP who spoke today. Then they whipped their MPs to vote against what their consciences were telling them.
veracity.explanation: Accurately reflects Luxon's public description of the Bill as divisive and National's whip to support only at first reading.

veracity.statement: Yesterday, the Harbour Bridge literally swayed with the power of the people as thousands marched for Te Tiriti,
veracity.explanation: 'literally swayed' is hyperbole; large marches occurred but the bridge-sway claim is embellishment.

rigor.statement: The Prime Minister has told us that there’s nothing that he likes about this Bill, calling it ‘divisive’ himself. He has told us the National Party do not support this Bill, as did every other National MP who spoke today. Then they whipped their MPs to vote against what their consciences were telling them.
rigor.explanation: Builds a hypocrisy argument from quoted positions; the 'against their consciences' step is inference rather than established fact.

charisma.statement: Today a majority of powerful people prioritised cynical politics, fanning the flame of a culture war, over the truth and the needs of our nation,
charisma.explanation: Rallies her own side with us-vs-them framing rather than building consensus.

specificity.statement: The decisions of the Minister, like cutting 400 jobs from OT and cutting funding to safety organisations, have resulted in an increase of urgent and critical reports of concern.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete decisions (400 OT jobs, funding cuts) and a claimed outcome.

veracity.statement: The decisions of the Minister, like cutting 400 jobs from OT and cutting funding to safety organisations, have resulted in an increase of urgent and critical reports of concern.
veracity.explanation: The OT job-cut figure is broadly reported; the causal claim about reports of concern is harder to substantiate.

rigor.statement: The decisions of the Minister, like cutting 400 jobs from OT and cutting funding to safety organisations, have resulted in an increase of urgent and critical reports of concern.
rigor.explanation: Asserts causation between the cuts and rising reports of concern without establishing the causal link.

specificity.statement: Visitors from 60 countries are currently able to access Aotearoa without a visa – not a single one of those countries is a Pacific Island country.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figure and a precise, checkable contrast.

specificity.statement: Aotearoa is part of the family of Pacific nations, and we must remove unfair barriers to entry for our Pacific whānau,
specificity.explanation: States a goal (remove barriers) but no mechanism or detail in this sentence.

veracity.statement: Visitors from 60 countries are currently able to access Aotearoa without a visa – not a single one of those countries is a Pacific Island country.
veracity.explanation: NZ's visa-waiver list does span roughly 60 countries and excludes Pacific Island states; accurate.

rigor.statement: Visitors from 60 countries are currently able to access Aotearoa without a visa – not a single one of those countries is a Pacific Island country.
rigor.explanation: Uses a factual comparison to support the fairness argument.

charisma.statement: Aotearoa is part of the family of Pacific nations, and we must remove unfair barriers to entry for our Pacific whānau,
charisma.explanation: Inclusive 'family of nations' framing, warm but appeals to a shared value.

specificity.statement: The repeated cuts across the country are a direct consequence of the Government’s decision to underfund the sector and have resulted in a reduction of classes, teachers and support for people trying to build their skills.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete effects (fewer classes, teachers, support) but no figures.

civility.statement: It’s time for the Minister for Vocational Education and Training to step up and support polytechs–not throw them to the wolves like she has so far,
civility.explanation: 'throw them to the wolves' is a pointed jab but aimed at the Minister's policy conduct rather than personal character.

rigor.statement: The repeated cuts across the country are a direct consequence of the Government’s decision to underfund the sector and have resulted in a reduction of classes, teachers and support for people trying to build their skills.
rigor.explanation: Asserts a direct causal chain from funding to cuts; plausible but the causation is stated rather than demonstrated.

veracity.statement: The percentage of electric vehicles coming into the country has plummeted since the Government repealed the Clean Car Discount,
veracity.explanation: EV registrations did fall sharply after the Clean Car Discount was scrapped in early 2024; accurate.

veracity.statement: The EV Leadership Group established by former National Transport Minister Simon Bridges recommended this FBT exclusion policy, and National campaigned on this very policy in opposition in 2020.
veracity.explanation: References a specific, checkable National-linked origin for the policy; broadly consistent with the record.

rigor.statement: The EV Leadership Group established by former National Transport Minister Simon Bridges recommended this FBT exclusion policy, and National campaigned on this very policy in opposition in 2020.
rigor.explanation: Uses the opponent's own prior endorsement as evidence the policy is reasonable — a coherent argument.

rigor.statement: The majority of new vehicles imported into New Zealand are purchased by businesses, and incentivising employers will mean more EVs will become available in the second-hand market so ordinary New Zealanders can access them.
rigor.explanation: Reasonable premise-to-conclusion chain (fleet turnover feeds the used market), though the scale of effect is asserted.

divination.statement: The majority of new vehicles imported into New Zealand are purchased by businesses, and incentivising employers will mean more EVs will become available in the second-hand market so ordinary New Zealanders can access them.
divination.explanation: Predicts more second-hand EV availability from employer incentives; directionally plausible but magnitude and timing unquantified.

strength.statement: This Bill would also build on the progress the Greens made last term when the Labour Government adopted an amendment of mine that saw bicycles, electric bicycles, and other low emissions transport from fringe benefit tax when used for commuting. This came after we secured an exemption for public transport passes.
strength.explanation: Cites specific measures she previously got enacted (FBT exemptions for active/public transport), demonstrated delivery.

authenticity.statement: This Bill would also build on the progress the Greens made last term when the Labour Government adopted an amendment of mine that saw bicycles, electric bicycles, and other low emissions transport from fringe benefit tax when used for commuting. This came after we secured an exemption for public transport passes.
authenticity.explanation: Her push for this EV Bill is consistent with a documented prior record of securing related FBT exemptions.

specificity.statement: From the start, I have always said my child is my priority. My tamaiti asked me to leave Parliament, and I am leaving for them and for my own wellbeing.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete reason for the decision, though personal rather than policy detail.

specificity.statement: Our politics, our democracy and our Parliament should be a place for everyone.
specificity.explanation: Broad platitude with no mechanism.

charisma.statement: Our politics, our democracy and our Parliament should be a place for everyone.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive aspiration, but general and appeals to a shared value without a concrete bridge-building ask.

authenticity.statement: From the start, I have always said my child is my priority. My tamaiti asked me to leave Parliament, and I am leaving for them and for my own wellbeing.
authenticity.explanation: Acts consistently with a stated long-held priority (child first) by actually resigning; words match the decision.

specificity.statement: Dame Tariana Turia was behind the Government’s adoption of the concept of Whānau Ora, was steadfast during the heinous Foreshore and Seabed debate in 2004, contributed years of work towards a Smokefree Aotearoa, and frequently showed, instead of just telling, her deep commitments to improving the lives of many in Aotearoa.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete policies and events, though as a tribute rather than a detailed account.

veracity.statement: Dame Tariana Turia was behind the Government’s adoption of the concept of Whānau Ora, was steadfast during the heinous Foreshore and Seabed debate in 2004, contributed years of work towards a Smokefree Aotearoa, and frequently showed, instead of just telling, her deep commitments to improving the lives of many in Aotearoa.
veracity.explanation: Accurately summarises Turia's record on Whānau Ora, the 2004 Foreshore and Seabed split, and smokefree work.

charisma.statement: Kiingi Tuuheitia put kotahitanga on the national agenda, as our guiding star, to build the country we all deserve,
charisma.explanation: Unifying tribute invoking kotahitanga (unity) and a shared national aspiration.

charisma.statement: Our Green Budget is a statement: we stand for Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we stand on the right side of history and we stand against this Government
charisma.explanation: Us-vs-them framing ('stand against this Government', 'right side of history') that rallies its own side and alienates opponents rather than building consensus.

charisma.statement: We can do all of this and more by making this a one-term Government, by demanding the rich pay their fair share and by using Te Tiriti o Waitangi as the poutokomanawa of our whare ora
charisma.explanation: 'Making this a one-term Government' is a partisan rallying cry, not a bridge-building appeal.

specificity.statement: Our Green Budget is a statement: we stand for Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we stand on the right side of history and we stand against this Government
specificity.explanation: A values slogan with no policy mechanism, figure, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: We will fill the gaps in our health system that have failed our people across generations by bringing back Te Aka Whai Ora and rolling out free GPs across the motu, especially in hard to reach communities.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete actions (reinstating the Māori Health Authority, free GPs) but no cost, funding, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: Our Hoki Whenua Mai policy means land back for tangata whenua and protection against further takings from the Crown.
specificity.explanation: Names a policy and its intent but gives no mechanism, scope, or timeline for how land return would occur.

specificity.statement: We can do all of this and more by making this a one-term Government, by demanding the rich pay their fair share and by using Te Tiriti o Waitangi as the poutokomanawa of our whare ora
specificity.explanation: 'Rich pay their fair share' is a direction with no tax rates, thresholds, or figures.

civility.statement: Our Green Budget is a statement: we stand for Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we stand on the right side of history and we stand against this Government
civility.explanation: Oppositional but aimed at the Government's stance rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: We have seen this Government undo decades of progress with endless assaults on our people and the lands we live on, all for the benefit of a wealthy few.
civility.explanation: 'Endless assaults' and 'benefit of a wealthy few' is sensationalist, emotive framing rather than substantive policy critique.

rigor.statement: We have seen this Government undo decades of progress with endless assaults on our people and the lands we live on, all for the benefit of a wealthy few.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping claim with no evidence cited; leans on emotive appeal ('assaults') and a wealthy-few trope.

veracity.statement: We have seen this Government undo decades of progress with endless assaults on our people and the lands we live on, all for the benefit of a wealthy few.
veracity.explanation: Hyperbolic ('endless assaults', 'undo decades of progress') and unquantified, making it more rhetorical than verifiable.

strength.statement: We will fill the gaps in our health system that have failed our people across generations by bringing back Te Aka Whai Ora and rolling out free GPs across the motu, especially in hard to reach communities.
strength.explanation: Opposition-party aspiration; Te Aka Whai Ora was disestablished by the current Government and the Greens are not in a position to deliver this.

specificity.statement: Families in Aotearoa face some of the highest ECE costs in the world. A lot of families pay around $10,000 a year per child – making ECE the biggest household cost after housing for many.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete annual figure and a comparative ranking of the household cost.

specificity.statement: We will initially cap charges at $10 per day per child on top of the current 20-hour free entitlement. This represents a significant shift from the $12 an-hour some families currently pay. By 2029, we will make ECE free by raising the entitlement to 35 hours a week.
specificity.explanation: Precise: dollar cap, comparison figure, target year (2029), and the exact hour entitlement.

civility.statement: One of the main reasons for this is corporate greed. Too much money meant for our children disappears into corporate profits, while parents pay sky-high fees and teachers earn far too little.
civility.explanation: Targets 'corporate' actors on policy/structure rather than a person, but 'greed' is loaded framing.

rigor.statement: One of the main reasons for this is corporate greed. Too much money meant for our children disappears into corporate profits, while parents pay sky-high fees and teachers earn far too little.
rigor.explanation: Attributes high costs to 'corporate greed' — an emotive, single-cause claim without evidence linking profit margins to fee levels.

veracity.statement: Families in Aotearoa face some of the highest ECE costs in the world. A lot of families pay around $10,000 a year per child – making ECE the biggest household cost after housing for many.
veracity.explanation: NZ ECE costs are indeed high by OECD comparison and ~$10k/year is plausible for full-time care; broadly accurate though 'some of the highest in the world' is at the upper end of the evidence.

veracity.statement: One of the main reasons for this is corporate greed. Too much money meant for our children disappears into corporate profits, while parents pay sky-high fees and teachers earn far too little.
veracity.explanation: For-profit chains do take public subsidies and some fees are high, but 'corporate greed' as 'one of the main reasons' oversimplifies a mixed sector.

veracity.statement: A large portion of the Government's funding for ECE goes straight into the pockets of for-profit chains. These for-profit providers benefit from hundreds of millions in public subsidies while charging high fees and paying low wages to teachers
veracity.explanation: For-profit ECE providers do receive substantial public subsidies and the sector has documented pay and fee issues; 'straight into the pockets' is loaded but the underlying facts are broadly supportable.

strength.statement: We will initially cap charges at $10 per day per child on top of the current 20-hour free entitlement. This represents a significant shift from the $12 an-hour some families currently pay. By 2029, we will make ECE free by raising the entitlement to 35 hours a week.
strength.explanation: Detailed and committed, but a policy proposal from opposition with no delivery; scored for stated intent only.

specificity.statement: A Green Government will rapidly reduce emissions, reduce the cost of living and improve our quality of life.
specificity.explanation: Three broad goals with no targets, mechanisms, or timeframes.

specificity.statement: That means free GP visits, free Early Childhood Education, free dental care, an Income Guarantee to ensure no one falls below the poverty line, housing for all, a stable climate, clean air, clean water and clean soil.
specificity.explanation: Lists named policies (free GPs, free ECE, free dental, Income Guarantee) but strings them as goals without costings or delivery detail.

civility.statement: Or, we can continue to let our infrastructure crumble, kids go hungry and the healthcare system teeter on the edge of collapse, as the Government promises for their Budget next week.
civility.explanation: Characterises the Government as choosing crumbling infrastructure and hungry kids — a sensationalised strawman of their Budget.

rigor.statement: Or, we can continue to let our infrastructure crumble, kids go hungry and the healthcare system teeter on the edge of collapse, as the Government promises for their Budget next week.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy (Green vision vs. total collapse) plus emotive catastrophising ('teeter on the edge of collapse') with no evidence.

veracity.statement: the Luxon Government's choices seeing New Zealanders leaving in record numbers
veracity.explanation: Net migration loss of NZ citizens did hit record highs around 2024; attributing it solely to Government 'choices' is contestable but the record-departures claim is broadly accurate.

strength.statement: A Green Government will rapidly reduce emissions, reduce the cost of living and improve our quality of life.
strength.explanation: Sweeping aspiration conditional on being in government; no delivery mechanism.

divination.statement: Or, we can continue to let our infrastructure crumble, kids go hungry and the healthcare system teeter on the edge of collapse, as the Government promises for their Budget next week.
divination.explanation: Predicts collapse/deterioration under the Government's Budget; catastrophic framing not well supported.

specificity.statement: A shocking 44 percent of Māori have an unmet need for primary care.
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete statistic tied to a defined population.

specificity.statement: We will create community care clinics in the highest need areas first, such as South Auckland, which has an estimated shortage of about 127 GPs.
specificity.explanation: Names the mechanism (community clinics), a priority area (South Auckland), and a specific estimated GP shortage figure.

rigor.statement: Free GP visits will reduce the pressure our hospitals are under by stopping small issues becoming big ones that need emergency treatment.
rigor.explanation: Plausible causal chain consistent with health-economics evidence, but asserted without citing data.

veracity.statement: A shocking 44 percent of Māori have an unmet need for primary care.
veracity.explanation: NZ Health Survey data show high unmet primary-care need among Māori; a figure in this range is plausible though the exact percentage depends on the measure and year.

divination.statement: Free GP visits will reduce the pressure our hospitals are under by stopping small issues becoming big ones that need emergency treatment.
divination.explanation: Predicts reduced hospital pressure from free primary care; directionally supported by evidence on preventable acute presentations, though magnitude is uncertain.

authenticity.statement: In the last election, we campaigned on providing free dental for all. Today, we're expanding that to ensure nobody is priced out of receiving the care they need, whether that is from the dentist or the doctor.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with the Greens' prior campaign position on free dental; presents an expansion of a stated policy rather than a reversal.

charisma.statement: The industry is on notice: consents granted under this regime that shortcut our democracy, sidestep environmental protections and degrade te taiao will be revoked by a Green Government
charisma.explanation: 'The industry is on notice' is combative and adversarial rather than consensus-building.

specificity.statement: The industry is on notice: consents granted under this regime that shortcut our democracy, sidestep environmental protections and degrade te taiao will be revoked by a Green Government
specificity.explanation: Concrete commitment (revoke consents) but the criteria for which consents remain broadly described.

civility.statement: This legislation is our out-of-touch Government's gift to Kiwis to digest while they enjoy their summer in the stunning natural environment, knowing so much of it is now open to private interests to develop it under fast-track for the sake of making a quick buck.
civility.explanation: 'Out-of-touch Government' and 'making a quick buck' are sarcastic, sensationalised jabs rather than substantive critique.

rigor.statement: This legislation is our out-of-touch Government's gift to Kiwis to digest while they enjoy their summer in the stunning natural environment, knowing so much of it is now open to private interests to develop it under fast-track for the sake of making a quick buck.
rigor.explanation: Emotive framing ('gift to Kiwis', 'quick buck') substitutes for evidence about the legislation's effects.

rigor.statement: New Zealanders do not want or deserve the environmental destruction this legislation looks set to unleash.
rigor.explanation: Asserts a collective public will and catastrophic outcome without evidence.

veracity.statement: Cabinet has approved a raft of projects said to have 'significant national or regional benefits' despite companies failing to even bother answering this question in their application.
veracity.explanation: A specific procedural claim about incomplete applications; plausible and pointed, but not verifiable from the text and phrased tendentiously ('bother').

veracity.statement: Companies who are meant to disclose their track record of prior compliance or enforcement actions against them, have in numerous cases failed to do so.
veracity.explanation: A concrete factual allegation about disclosure failures; credible but unsubstantiated within the text.

strength.statement: The industry is on notice: consents granted under this regime that shortcut our democracy, sidestep environmental protections and degrade te taiao will be revoked by a Green Government

divination.statement: New Zealanders do not want or deserve the environmental destruction this legislation looks set to unleash.
divination.explanation: Predicts environmental destruction from the fast-track regime; directionally arguable but 'unleash' overstates certainty of outcome.

specificity.explanation: Clear, concrete commitments (reinstate ban, revoke permits), though 'fossil fuel-obsessed' is rhetorical.

specificity.statement: Climate delay is the new denial.
specificity.explanation: A rhetorical slogan with no concrete content.

civility.statement: Luxon's Government has weaponised the energy crisis to argue for more fossil fuels, conveniently neglecting that it's the very reliance on those fossil fuels which is behind the energy crisis.
civility.explanation: 'Weaponised' and 'conveniently neglecting' impute bad faith, but the critique is aimed at the argument/policy rather than personal character.

rigor.statement: Overturning the oil and gas ban risks exacerbating energy insecurity and driving exorbitant power prices.
rigor.explanation: A reasoned argument tying reliance on fossil fuels to price volatility, but stated as risk without supporting data.

rigor.statement: Luxon's Government has weaponised the energy crisis to argue for more fossil fuels, conveniently neglecting that it's the very reliance on those fossil fuels which is behind the energy crisis.
rigor.explanation: Makes a coherent causal point (dependence on gas drives the crisis) but frames the opponent's motive rather than engaging their reasoning.

strength.statement: A Green Government will reinstate the oil and gas ban and revoke any permits granted under the current fossil fuel-obsessed regime
strength.explanation: Consistent with the Greens' record (the ban originated under the previous government they were part of), but delivery depends on returning to power.

divination.statement: Overturning the oil and gas ban risks exacerbating energy insecurity and driving exorbitant power prices.
divination.explanation: Predicts worsened energy security and higher prices from reopening exploration; contested — new gas supply could equally be argued to ease prices, so evidence is mixed.

authenticity.statement: A Green Government will reinstate the oil and gas ban and revoke any permits granted under the current fossil fuel-obsessed regime
authenticity.explanation: Aligns with the party's long-held anti-fossil-fuel position and support for the original 2018 exploration ban.

specificity.statement: The Bill describes te mana o te tohorā through five fundamental principles: Freedom of movement and migration, protection of natural behaviours, protection of social and cultural structures, right to a healthy environment, and the right to restoration and regeneration of habits and ecosystems.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates five defined principles the Bill would enshrine; concrete legislative content.

specificity.statement: This Bill represents a transformation in how we protect our marine species and the wider moana, to create a law that would protect whales by legally recognising their mana.
specificity.explanation: States the aim (legal personhood/mana for whales) but 'a transformation' is aspirational framing rather than operational detail.

veracity.statement: Our tohorā are sacred ancestors for many communities across Te Moana Nui a Kiwa, but they are under threat from commercial fishing, pollution, and climate change.
veracity.explanation: Whales do face documented threats from fishing bycatch/entanglement, pollution and climate change; accurate general claim.

specificity.statement: Having served as a Green City Councillor for fourteen years, two terms as Mayor, and a Green Party list MP, I will continue to strongly support the Green Party
specificity.explanation: Gives concrete tenure details, though the forward commitment ('continue to support') is general.

specificity.statement: I hope to progress my Domestic Cat Microchipping members bill which will improve domestic cat welfare and reduce harm to native species.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific bill and its two intended effects, though 'hope to progress' is tentative.

civility.statement: Celia has given many decades to improving outcomes for Wellingtonians and te taiao as part of the Green Party. She is a champion for a sustainable living in local and central government.
civility.explanation: Warm, respectful acknowledgement of a colleague's contribution; entirely constructive.

veracity.statement: Having served as a Green City Councillor for fourteen years, two terms as Mayor, and a Green Party list MP, I will continue to strongly support the Green Party
veracity.explanation: Wade-Brown's record as a Wellington councillor, two-term Mayor and Green list MP is accurate and verifiable.

strength.statement: I hope to progress my Domestic Cat Microchipping members bill which will improve domestic cat welfare and reduce harm to native species.
strength.explanation: A concrete legislative goal with cross-party interest noted, but as yet undelivered and only aspired to.

charisma.statement: I call on parties across the House to get behind this Bill at its First Reading early next year.
charisma.explanation: An explicit cross-party appeal to support the Bill, seeking consensus beyond the Greens.

specificity.statement: it's clear we need to bring our law up to date, and into line with the laws of other developed countries, including Australia, the United States, Belgium, France, the Netherlands, Spain, and Germany.
specificity.explanation: Names the reform (parody/satire copyright exception) and lists specific comparator countries.

specificity.statement: This Bill protects artists' right to freedom of speech, and in doing so helps protect our democracy. Humour is essential to a thriving democracy, with both parody and satire playing a critical role in public discourse.
specificity.explanation: States the Bill's rationale but in broad democratic-value terms rather than legal mechanism.

rigor.statement: it's clear we need to bring our law up to date, and into line with the laws of other developed countries, including Australia, the United States, Belgium, France, the Netherlands, Spain, and Germany.
rigor.explanation: Argues by comparison to peer countries — a reasonable but partly appeal-to-others'-practice basis for reform.

rigor.statement: This Bill protects artists' right to freedom of speech, and in doing so helps protect our democracy. Humour is essential to a thriving democracy, with both parody and satire playing a critical role in public discourse.
rigor.explanation: A reasonable free-speech argument, but the leap from a copyright exception to 'protecting democracy' is asserted rather than demonstrated.

veracity.statement: it's clear we need to bring our law up to date, and into line with the laws of other developed countries, including Australia, the United States, Belgium, France, the Netherlands, Spain, and Germany.

charisma.statement: We are going to do everything in our power to make this a one term government.
charisma.explanation: Purely combative partisan aim; makes no attempt to persuade or include opponents.

specificity.statement: We defied history in this election with a record 330,883 people voting for the Green Party.
specificity.explanation: Cites an exact vote count.

specificity.statement: Now more than ever, we need to be taking bold action to build a cleaner, fairer climate friendly future where everyone can afford a warm home and food on the table.
specificity.explanation: Aspirational language ('bold action', 'cleaner, fairer future') without concrete measures.

civility.statement: National, Act, and New Zealand First have shown their willingness to do and say anything to get into power.
civility.explanation: Broad impugning of three parties' integrity ('say anything') — a character-based attack rather than policy critique.

civility.statement: The plan to allow state schools to transition to partnership schools and make it easier for people to access guns, is completely out of touch with what New Zealand needs.
civility.explanation: 'Completely out of touch' is a dismissive judgement but attached to specific policies rather than a person.

rigor.statement: National, Act, and New Zealand First have shown their willingness to do and say anything to get into power.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping generalisation with no supporting evidence.

veracity.statement: We defied history in this election with a record 330,883 people voting for the Green Party.
veracity.explanation: The Greens' 2023 party vote was a record high for the party, in the region of this figure; accurate.

veracity.statement: The plan to allow state schools to transition to partnership schools and make it easier for people to access guns, is completely out of touch with what New Zealand needs.
veracity.explanation: The coalition did agree to reinstate charter/partnership schools and to review firearms law; the factual basis is broadly accurate, though 'easier to access guns' characterises the intent.

veracity.statement: I am delighted to be heading into the next term of Parliament with the biggest caucus we have ever had
veracity.explanation: The Greens' 15 MPs after 2023 was their largest-ever caucus; accurate.

strength.statement: We are going to do everything in our power to make this a one term government.
strength.explanation: An aspiration dependent on the electorate, not something within the party's direct power to deliver.

specificity.statement: Bold Māori voices will ensure that we can build a government that upholds te Tiriti o Waitangi and honours the Crown's responsibility to guarantee tino rangatiratanga of tangata whenua over their whenua, kāinga and taonga katoa.
specificity.explanation: States a constitutional aspiration but no concrete policy, mechanism, or timeframe.

charisma.statement: The Green Party stands with support staff in their call for a fair and equitable resolution that reflects the essential role they play in the education sector.

specificity.statement: The Green Party stands with support staff in their call for a fair and equitable resolution that reflects the essential role they play in the education sector.
specificity.explanation: General expression of solidarity with no specific pay figure or demand attached.

civility.statement: This appalling offer is a slap in the face to the essential support staff who keep our schools running
civility.explanation: Emotive ('slap in the face') and critical of the offer rather than a person; harsh but policy-directed.

veracity.statement: He has stood by and watched as Treaty protections were removed from state care, as the Māori Health Authority was scrapped and as Māori wards were essentially erased.

specificity.statement: He has stood by and watched as Treaty protections were removed from state care, as the Māori Health Authority was scrapped and as Māori wards were essentially erased.

specificity.statement: Upholding Te Tiriti is about rectifying the wrongs of our past, challenging the injustices of our present, and building a country that provides for everybody,
specificity.explanation: Broad value statement with no concrete mechanism or measure.

civility.statement: At Waitangi, Christopher Luxon told Māori that Te Tiriti was our past, present and future. If he truly meant what he said, he would not allow someone to attempt to re-write our history with such a lack of understanding and regard for this nation's founding agreement.
civility.explanation: Challenges the PM's consistency with a direct quote rather than name-calling, though it questions his sincerity.

charisma.statement: Upholding Te Tiriti is about rectifying the wrongs of our past, challenging the injustices of our present, and building a country that provides for everybody,
charisma.explanation: Inclusive 'provides for everybody' framing that seeks a unifying vision.

authenticity.statement: At Waitangi, Christopher Luxon told Māori that Te Tiriti was our past, present and future. If he truly meant what he said, he would not allow someone to attempt to re-write our history with such a lack of understanding and regard for this nation's founding agreement.
authenticity.explanation: Directed at Luxon: highlights an alleged gap between his Waitangi words and tolerance of the Bill — a low-authenticity signal about the opponent, not the speaker.

specificity.statement: Currently, the maximum amount available is just $400. It hasn't been updated in at least 13 years, despite the much higher cost of living.

specificity.statement: We intend to keep the pressure on the Government to double the payment and expand its availability to all affected regions.

civility.statement: While we welcome the Civil Defence Payment, the Government needs to increase the payment and make it available to all regions affected by the extreme weather events

authenticity.statement: We wrote to the Prime Minister earlier this week and we're glad that pressure worked.

veracity.statement: The Waitangi Tribunal, translation specialists, iwi leaders, historians and now more than 400 Christian leaders have been clear that the Treaty Principles Bill distorts the true meaning of Te Tiriti while failing to uphold the rights Māori were promised as part of it.

rigor.explanation: Marshals multiple expert/authority sources; persuasive by breadth but relies on appeal to authority rather than direct argument.

specificity.statement: The Waitangi Tribunal, translation specialists, iwi leaders, historians and now more than 400 Christian leaders have been clear that the Treaty Principles Bill distorts the true meaning of Te Tiriti while failing to uphold the rights Māori were promised as part of it.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates categories of critics and a number (400) but the objection is stated generally.

civility.statement: The Prime Minister's actions need to match his words. He cannot stand at Waitangi and say that Te Tiriti is our past, present and future and then let legislation that corrupts the very meaning of the Treaty to progress through our Parliament.
civility.explanation: Criticises the contradiction using his own words; firm but not a personal insult.

authenticity.statement: The Prime Minister's actions need to match his words. He cannot stand at Waitangi and say that Te Tiriti is our past, present and future and then let legislation that corrupts the very meaning of the Treaty to progress through our Parliament.
authenticity.explanation: Aimed at Luxon: alleges a words-vs-actions inconsistency between his Waitangi speech and permitting the Bill — a low-authenticity signal about the opponent.

veracity.statement: This Court of Appeal decision upholds the principle that public land belongs to New Zealanders and our wildlife,
veracity.explanation: Reasonable characterisation of the Court of Appeal ruling, though 'belongs to... wildlife' is rhetorical framing of the legal finding.

rigor.statement: Mining leaves the burden of the environmental destruction on locals and future generations of regular people, but the benefits are largely restricted to the off-shore deep-pocketed big corporates.
rigor.explanation: A cost/benefit distribution argument; plausible but sweeping and unquantified, casting all mining benefit as off-shore.

civility.statement: Mining leaves the burden of the environmental destruction on locals and future generations of regular people, but the benefits are largely restricted to the off-shore deep-pocketed big corporates.

veracity.statement: With a larger share of the vote and more MPs than we've had before, Green Party will lead the ongoing fight to eliminate poverty, honour Te Tiriti, protect nature, and build a climate-resilient future for our mokopuna,

veracity.statement: Half our Caucus is now Maori and Pasifika, which is a huge step forward for us. We are also proud to be joined by the first Member of Parliament in Aotearoa who is Vietnamese.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with the Greens' 2023 caucus composition and the election of NZ's first Vietnamese-heritage MP.

veracity.statement: We are the only support party in the history of MMP to have grown our vote during a term in Government - and we have done it twice now.
veracity.explanation: Broadly accurate that Greens grew their vote after governing terms; a strong self-comparative claim generally supported by MMP results.

veracity.statement: We also ran one of the biggest grassroots campaigns we have ever had. 280,000 door knocks & phone calls, 90,000 meaningful convos with voters across New Zealand, and 7,700 volunteers.
veracity.explanation: Internal campaign metrics not independently verifiable but plausible and specific; scored as credible self-report.

specificity.statement: With a larger share of the vote and more MPs than we've had before, Green Party will lead the ongoing fight to eliminate poverty, honour Te Tiriti, protect nature, and build a climate-resilient future for our mokopuna,
specificity.explanation: Lists broad goal areas without mechanisms or measures.

specificity.statement: Half our Caucus is now Maori and Pasifika, which is a huge step forward for us. We are also proud to be joined by the first Member of Parliament in Aotearoa who is Vietnamese.
specificity.explanation: Concrete claims about caucus makeup and a historical first.

specificity.statement: We are the only support party in the history of MMP to have grown our vote during a term in Government - and we have done it twice now.

specificity.statement: Our campaign inspired hope, rather than fear, and focused on thoroughly thought through, long-term policy, not just soundbites.

specificity.explanation: Multiple precise figures for outreach and volunteers.

specificity.statement: over the next three years, the Green Party will be a strong and unwavering voice for climate action, for the protection of our native wildlife, and for ensuring that every New Zealander has enough to live with dignity,
specificity.explanation: Commits to being 'a voice' over a term but names no policies, measures, or targets.

charisma.statement: Our campaign inspired hope, rather than fear, and focused on thoroughly thought through, long-term policy, not just soundbites.
charisma.explanation: Hope-over-fear framing is aspirational, but implicitly contrasts against opponents and speaks mainly to supporters.

strength.statement: over the next three years, the Green Party will be a strong and unwavering voice for climate action, for the protection of our native wildlife, and for ensuring that every New Zealander has enough to live with dignity,
strength.explanation: Rhetorical commitment to advocacy rather than a deliverable policy.

veracity.statement: The Special Authority process currently requires someone with ADHD to go back to a psychiatrist every two years to confirm they still have ADHD. This has been clearly identified time and again as a major cost and barrier to accessing treatment.
veracity.explanation: Accurately describes the special authority renewal requirement Pharmac consulted on removing.

veracity.statement: New Zealanders with ADHD have also long been denied treatments funded in comparable jurisdictions like Australia.
veracity.explanation: Lisdexamfetamine and similar treatments were funded in Australia but not NZ at the time; broadly accurate.

rigor.statement: The Special Authority process currently requires someone with ADHD to go back to a psychiatrist every two years to confirm they still have ADHD. This has been clearly identified time and again as a major cost and barrier to accessing treatment.
rigor.explanation: Identifies a concrete barrier and links it to under-treatment; reasoned though the 'many go without' consequence is asserted.

specificity.statement: The Special Authority process currently requires someone with ADHD to go back to a psychiatrist every two years to confirm they still have ADHD. This has been clearly identified time and again as a major cost and barrier to accessing treatment.
specificity.explanation: Describes the exact mechanism (two-year psychiatrist renewal) and its effect.

charisma.statement: It has been a personal and political honour to work alongside our neurodivergent community and our advocates, across the House and Governments of different stripes, to secure the most significant steps forward in decades for those living with ADHD.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly credits cross-party work ('across the House and Governments of different stripes') and community advocates — inclusive and consensus-building.

strength.statement: It has been a personal and political honour to work alongside our neurodivergent community and our advocates, across the House and Governments of different stripes, to secure the most significant steps forward in decades for those living with ADHD.
strength.explanation: Claims credit for securing Pharmac consultation; a genuine step but a consultation announcement rather than final funding delivered.

veracity.statement: Current tax settings allow multi-millionaires to pay only $9 in tax out of every $100 they make, while a teacher pays $22 in tax out of every $100 they earn.
veracity.explanation: Echoes the 2023 IRD high-wealth study (effective rate ~9-10% including capital gains); the teacher comparison mixes bases, slightly apples-to-oranges but directionally supported.

veracity.statement: They know that while their cost of living has gone through the roof, corporate profits have skyrocketed and the wealthiest 150 rich listers now own more than half of the country.
veracity.explanation: 'own more than half of the country' is a significant exaggeration; the Rich List holds large wealth but nowhere near half of national wealth.

veracity.statement: Right now, Facebook, Google, Amazon and other multinational corporations are being allowed to make billions out of New Zealanders and pay next to nothing in tax for it, while small, local businesses are chased by the IRD into liquidation.
veracity.explanation: Large multinationals do book low NZ tax relative to revenue, but 'pay next to nothing' and the liquidation contrast are hyperbolic.

veracity.statement: New Zealand's economy is the largest it's ever been, with record profits being made by some. Yet the cost of living is through the roof for ordinary people, and our hospitals, schools, public transport, and environment are all starved of funding.
veracity.explanation: Nominal GDP at a record is trivially true; 'record profits' and 'starved of funding' are selective framing omitting context.

veracity.statement: Instead, homelessness, unemployment, and poverty are increasing – while banks, the supermarket duopoly, power companies, and big tech make massive profits.
veracity.explanation: Unemployment and homelessness measures rose over this period and the named sectors are high-profit; broadly supported though 'poverty increasing' depends on measure.

rigor.statement: Current tax settings allow multi-millionaires to pay only $9 in tax out of every $100 they make, while a teacher pays $22 in tax out of every $100 they earn.
rigor.explanation: Uses evidence-based figures but the two rates are not calculated on strictly identical bases, a gap in the comparison.

rigor.statement: Right now, Facebook, Google, Amazon and other multinational corporations are being allowed to make billions out of New Zealanders and pay next to nothing in tax for it, while small, local businesses are chased by the IRD into liquidation.

rigor.statement: New Zealand's economy is the largest it's ever been, with record profits being made by some. Yet the cost of living is through the roof for ordinary people, and our hospitals, schools, public transport, and environment are all starved of funding.

specificity.statement: Right now, Facebook, Google, Amazon and other multinational corporations are being allowed to make billions out of New Zealanders and pay next to nothing in tax for it, while small, local businesses are chased by the IRD into liquidation.

charisma.statement: Aotearoa is part of the family of Pacific nations. We must remove unfair barriers to entry for our Pacific whānau,

civility.statement: Christopher Luxon today waved goodbye to record numbers of New Zealanders leaving the country as he offers nothing but reheated austerity

veracity.statement: Christopher Luxon today waved goodbye to record numbers of New Zealanders leaving the country as he offers nothing but reheated austerity

veracity.statement: The IRD tells us that the wealthiest 311 households hold more wealth combined than the bottom two and a half million, while paying half the effective tax rate of the average New Zealander.

veracity.statement: Rules reinforced by Luxon mean you can bank more money and avoid paying tax if you speculate on properties instead of working. That's the productivity problem.
veracity.explanation: NZ's lack of a capital gains tax does favour untaxed property gains, though 'reinforced by Luxon' overstates a longstanding settings issue.

charisma.statement: Christopher Luxon today waved goodbye to record numbers of New Zealanders leaving the country as he offers nothing but reheated austerity
charisma.explanation: Rallies her side against Luxon with no attempt to build consensus.

charisma.statement: We are a country of enormous talent that punches well above our weight. Let's invest in that, instead of hoping some billionaires will come and save us.

rigor.explanation: Contains a plausible argument (cutting R&D/infrastructure undermines growth) but relies on mocking framing ('magically') rather than cited evidence.

rigor.statement: To the closure of pulp and paper mills in Ohakune and Tokoroa. To the lack of any industrial planning to support miners out of a volatile boom and bust cycle.
rigor.explanation: Cites specific examples to support the claim about failed growth policy, though causation is asserted not demonstrated.

rigor.statement: Doing more of the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result is the definition of insanity.

rigor.statement: The IRD tells us that the wealthiest 311 households hold more wealth combined than the bottom two and a half million, while paying half the effective tax rate of the average New Zealander.

rigor.statement: Rules reinforced by Luxon mean you can bank more money and avoid paying tax if you speculate on properties instead of working. That's the productivity problem.

specificity.statement: The IRD tells us that the wealthiest 311 households hold more wealth combined than the bottom two and a half million, while paying half the effective tax rate of the average New Zealander.

civility.explanation: Critical of government action rather than a personal attack, but uses emotive framing.

civility.statement: In other words, their 'tough on crime' rhetoric once again serves no one other than the people in power.

rigor.statement: In other words, their 'tough on crime' rhetoric once again serves no one other than the people in power.

specificity.statement: Today the Government has taken us even further away from a justice system that treats everyone with humanity, dignity, and respect

specificity.statement: Right now, 60% of Māori in prison have been a victim of family violence - that's 2,400 people.

specificity.statement: Reducing the prison population can go hand-in-hand with reducing reoffending through using more suitable community based sentences that have better rehabilitative outcome.

specificity.statement: We need a government that will work toward a justice system that restores mana to our people and communities and heals the harms of intergenerational trauma.

civility.statement: This is a terrible outcome for Māori media, and sadly consistent with this Government's continual undermining of our culture
civility.explanation: Strong criticism of government pattern; not a personal attack but broadly accusatory.

civility.statement: Our media ecosystem is struggling in an environment of budget tightening under a Government which can find billions of dollars in tax cuts for landlords and tobacco companies but nothing for Māori news and current affairs.
civility.explanation: Attacks spending priorities rather than persons.

veracity.statement: Our media ecosystem is struggling in an environment of budget tightening under a Government which can find billions of dollars in tax cuts for landlords and tobacco companies but nothing for Māori news and current affairs.

veracity.statement: Te Karere has been delivering a quality national Māori news service on mainstream media for four decades.

rigor.statement: Our media ecosystem is struggling in an environment of budget tightening under a Government which can find billions of dollars in tax cuts for landlords and tobacco companies but nothing for Māori news and current affairs.

specificity.statement: This is a terrible outcome for Māori media, and sadly consistent with this Government's continual undermining of our culture
specificity.explanation: General characterisation without specific figures beyond the referenced cut.

specificity.statement: Te Karere has been delivering a quality national Māori news service on mainstream media for four decades.
specificity.explanation: Names the programme and a concrete timeframe.

specificity.statement: The Green Party would increase funding for a media network that is unapologetically Māori, enhancing regional collaboration and helping communities across the motu develop a sense of ownership in the programmes
specificity.explanation: States a direction (increase funding) but no amount, source or timeframe.

strength.statement: The Green Party would increase funding for a media network that is unapologetically Māori, enhancing regional collaboration and helping communities across the motu develop a sense of ownership in the programmes

civility.statement: Stealing from the future pay of some of the lowest paid women doing critical mahi is straight up disgusting!

civility.statement: Christopher Luxon is pouring oil and gas all over the climate crisis while fast-tracking the destruction of our natural world. This will inflame the climate crisis and impact heavily on our mokopuna both now and into their future.

veracity.statement: Dishing out billions of dollars of tax cuts to landlords while choosing to make more people homeless falls short of the promise this country was built on.

veracity.statement: Stealing from the future pay of some of the lowest paid women doing critical mahi is straight up disgusting!

charisma.statement: When we come together - grounded in care for each other and the whenua, and strengthened by diverse experiences, grounded in justice - we can change the course of our future and take ownership of it.

rigor.explanation: Sets up a words-vs-deeds contrast; the conclusion depends on subsequent examples she supplies.

rigor.statement: Christopher Luxon is pouring oil and gas all over the climate crisis while fast-tracking the destruction of our natural world. This will inflame the climate crisis and impact heavily on our mokopuna both now and into their future.
rigor.explanation: Emotive metaphor ('pouring oil and gas') substitutes for evidenced argument.

specificity.statement: With our emissions reduction plan, our Green Budget, our jobs strategy and our fiscal strategy, the Greens have laid a clear case for change and a bold vision for better.
specificity.explanation: Names four concrete Green documents but doesn't state their contents or figures here.

specificity.statement: Where we can ensure everyone in Aotearoa can get the care they need, when they need it, with free GPs and free dental.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete policies (free GPs, free dental) but no cost, funding source or timeframe.

specificity.statement: When we come together - grounded in care for each other and the whenua, and strengthened by diverse experiences, grounded in justice - we can change the course of our future and take ownership of it.
specificity.explanation: Inspirational but commits to nothing concrete.

specificity.statement: We're not here to just lead the opposition, we are here because we want to lead the next Government.
specificity.explanation: Clear, concrete statement of ambition.

strength.statement: With our emissions reduction plan, our Green Budget, our jobs strategy and our fiscal strategy, the Greens have laid a clear case for change and a bold vision for better.

strength.statement: Where we can ensure everyone in Aotearoa can get the care they need, when they need it, with free GPs and free dental.

charisma.statement: I believe in community – I believe in our collective strength, and my journey over the past year has made so clear how necessary it is to take care of others, and to be taken care of.

authenticity.statement: I believe in community – I believe in our collective strength, and my journey over the past year has made so clear how necessary it is to take care of others, and to be taken care of.

strength.statement: Consents that are granted under shoddy processes will be reviewed when the Greens are next in Government, and potential applicants should be aware that any consents which should not have been granted in the first place will be revoked.

specificity.statement: Kāinga Ora has been clear that these cuts are a result of them planning to build less housing at a time where more than 20,000 people across the country are waiting for a public home to become available.

specificity.statement: With Green, Te Pāti Māori and Labour’s committed support, we now need just six of 68 Government MPs to pass my Unlawful Occupation of Palestine Sanctions Bill into law.
specificity.explanation: Names the parties, the exact number of MPs needed (six of 68), and the named Bill and mechanism.

specificity.statement: In just the last 24 hours, Israel’s strikes on Gaza have killed at least 400 people, mostly children and women, and left many more injured.
specificity.explanation: Specific timeframe (24 hours) and casualty figure.

rigor.statement: Aotearoa New Zealand cannot remain a bystander to the slaughter of innocent people in Gaza. We can and must act now to sanction Israel for its crimes, just like we did with Russia for its illegal action in Ukraine.
rigor.explanation: Argues by analogy to NZ's Russia sanctions; a reasonable comparison but the analogy's fit (statutory basis differed) is asserted rather than established.

charisma.statement: No party leader or whip can stop a Member of Parliament exercising their democratic right to vote how they know they need to on this Bill. There is no more hiding behind party lines. All 123 Members of Parliament are each individually, personally responsible.
charisma.explanation: Directly appeals to individual government MPs' conscience to cross party lines — an attempt to persuade the other side, though framed as moral pressure.

specificity.statement: The US election result should be a wake-up call that our country must steer clear of the AUKUS military pact
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete policy (AUKUS) and a clear position (stay out), but no detail on mechanism or process.

specificity.statement: Aotearoa New Zealand must return to the independent and principled approach to foreign affairs that we were valued for in the international community. We should use that position to advance climate action, protect nature, advocate for indigenous and human rights, and global justice.
specificity.explanation: Broad values (climate, nature, human rights) with no concrete mechanism, target, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: Even if Pillar 2 is the so-called technology-only part of the agreement, it is still part of the same precarious project fixated on conflict with the west’s perceived enemies.
specificity.explanation: Engages the specific Pillar 2 distinction, though the conclusion stays at the level of characterisation.

specificity.statement: Let’s remain an advocate for diplomacy and dialogue, and pursue our independent voice in world affairs. That’s what other countries look to us for

civility.explanation: Policy-focused framing about a defence pact, no personal attack, though 'wake-up call' is mild rhetoric.

civility.explanation: Heavy characterisation ('volatile firebrand with fascist leanings') of an incoming foreign leader; personalised and hyperbolic rather than engaging policy substance.

civility.statement: Unfortunately, this Government is jeopardising our independent foreign policy voice and falling into line behind a march to conflict and great power antagonism that is reckless and unnecessary.

rigor.statement: Unfortunately, this Government is jeopardising our independent foreign policy voice and falling into line behind a march to conflict and great power antagonism that is reckless and unnecessary.

civility.statement: This Government has been incredibly slow to respond to the crisis in Gaza, it cannot afford to make the same mistake twice and allow the window for evacuations to close.

charisma.statement: We can have meaningful action that reduces emissions and the cost of living while improving all of our lives.

civility.explanation: Ascribes bad motive ('fanning the flames', 'targeting') to the Government rather than engaging the policy substance.

charisma.statement: Aotearoa can be a country that leads with compassion, evidence and aroha. charisma.statement: Once again, Luxon’s Government has espoused some incredibly transphobic rhetoric that aims to cause harm and division.
