charisma.statement: I also would like to acknowledge the previous Speakers, Trevor Mallard and Adrian Rurawhe for their work to make Parliament a better place, and their dignity in presiding over the house.
charisma.explanation: Bridge-building, respectful recognition of others.

charisma.statement: The Green Party is committed to working with the new Speaker towards continuing to make Parliament family friendly, protecting staff, accessibility across the precinct and honouring the duty of care members of this house have to each other,
charisma.explanation: Collaborative, institution-focused framing that reaches across the House.

veracity.statement: This is the first time in history that a Green MP has been appointed to this role, and it is an honour to serve Aotearoa's Parliament,
veracity.explanation: Accurate: first Green MP appointed Assistant Speaker.

civility.statement: This is the first time in history that a Green MP has been appointed to this role, and it is an honour to serve Aotearoa's Parliament,
civility.explanation: Gracious, respectful of the institution.

civility.statement: I would like to thank my colleagues across the house for my appointment, and their trust in me to do the job.
civility.explanation: Cross-party gratitude, wholly respectful.

civility.statement: I also would like to acknowledge the previous Speakers, Trevor Mallard and Adrian Rurawhe for their work to make Parliament a better place, and their dignity in presiding over the house.
civility.explanation: Generous acknowledgement of predecessors, including across party lines.

specificity.statement: Funnelling an additional $1 billion from this Budget into roads of National Party significance is ridiculous and irresponsible.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar figure and direction, no project detail.

specificity.statement: Investments that improve public transport, walking and biking cost far less, and have higher benefits - unlike vanity roading projects.
specificity.explanation: General direction, no figures or named projects.

rigor.statement: The Coalition Government is stuck in a time warp, obsessed with building a handful of expensive highways to take us back to the past with them,
rigor.explanation: Rhetorical 'time warp' framing rather than argument.

rigor.statement: The vast majority of the transport budget has been going to roads, that's why so many people have to use a car to get anywhere.
rigor.explanation: Draws a plausible but single-cause conclusion about car dependence.

rigor.statement: Investments that improve public transport, walking and biking cost far less, and have higher benefits - unlike vanity roading projects.
rigor.explanation: Cost-benefit claim has support in some appraisals but is asserted broadly; 'vanity' is loaded.

rigor.statement: This government wants to drive New Zealand back to the 1950s where simply adding lanes to urban highways guides our response to congestion
rigor.explanation: Strawman-flavoured characterisation rather than engagement with the actual policy rationale.

veracity.statement: The vast majority of the transport budget has been going to roads, that's why so many people have to use a car to get anywhere.
veracity.explanation: Roads have historically dominated NZ transport spending; the causal 'that's why' is simplified.

veracity.statement: Funnelling an additional $1 billion from this Budget into roads of National Party significance is ridiculous and irresponsible.
veracity.explanation: The $1b roading figure is broadly consistent with Budget 2024 roading allocations; 'of National Party significance' is a partisan gloss.

civility.statement: The Coalition Government is stuck in a time warp, obsessed with building a handful of expensive highways to take us back to the past with them,
civility.explanation: Mocking characterisation of the Government's priorities.

civility.statement: Funnelling an additional $1 billion from this Budget into roads of National Party significance is ridiculous and irresponsible.
civility.explanation: 'Ridiculous and irresponsible' criticises the choice sharply but not personally.

civility.statement: This government wants to drive New Zealand back to the 1950s where simply adding lanes to urban highways guides our response to congestion
civility.explanation: Caricatures the Government's approach as 1950s thinking.

divination.statement: We will be paying back these projects for decades, just to wind up stuck in traffic again.
divination.explanation: Predicts long-term debt and induced congestion; induced-demand evidence supports the direction but the outcome is uncertain.

specificity.statement: The Green Party will push every single day to make sure everyone has what they need to get by, that our children always have enough to eat, that our native wildlife and ocean thrives, and that Aotearoa is tackling climate change with the urgency it demands.
specificity.explanation: Broad aspirational list without mechanisms or measures.

specificity.statement: The Green Party will make sure the voices of workers are brought into Parliament in the face of the repeal of Fair Pay Agreements and re-introduction of harmful 90 day trials.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete policies at issue but the commitment ('make sure voices are brought in') is vague.

specificity.statement: We will fight to maintain the progress that we have made on climate change as the Clean Car Discount is scrapped.
specificity.explanation: References a specific policy being scrapped but the pledge to 'fight' is unspecified.

charisma.statement: for more than 30 years we have known better than anyone that there is only one way to change Aotearoa for the better - and that is together.
charisma.explanation: Invokes unity and collective action, an inclusive appeal.

rigor.statement: The random, visionless, and harmful grab bag of policies in the government's 100 day plan does not represent our future.
rigor.explanation: Adjective-driven assertion with no supporting evidence.

civility.statement: The random, visionless, and harmful grab bag of policies in the government's 100 day plan does not represent our future.
civility.explanation: Dismissive labelling of the whole plan without engaging specifics.

authenticity.statement: We will fight to maintain the progress that we have made on climate change as the Clean Car Discount is scrapped.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with Shaw's record as Climate Change Minister who championed such measures.

strength.statement: The Green Party will push every single day to make sure everyone has what they need to get by, that our children always have enough to eat, that our native wildlife and ocean thrives, and that Aotearoa is tackling climate change with the urgency it demands.
strength.explanation: Sweeping commitment from opposition with no concrete deliverable.

strength.statement: The Green Party will make sure the voices of workers are brought into Parliament in the face of the repeal of Fair Pay Agreements and re-introduction of harmful 90 day trials.
strength.explanation: Opposition advocacy pledge with no lever to deliver against the repeals.

specificity.statement: The HYEFU shows unemployment increasing next year–with everyday New Zealanders taking the hit.
specificity.explanation: Points to a specific indicator and document but no figures.

specificity.statement: New Zealanders need responsible fiscal management from our leaders–to manage the real economy, not just abstracted numbers on a page. Under a Green Government, people and planet come before profit, through a fairer tax system and a public investment in the infrastructure we–and our economy–needs.
specificity.explanation: Names directions (fairer tax, public investment) but no rates, amounts or targets.

charisma.statement: New Zealanders need responsible fiscal management from our leaders–to manage the real economy, not just abstracted numbers on a page. Under a Green Government, people and planet come before profit, through a fairer tax system and a public investment in the infrastructure we–and our economy–needs.
charisma.explanation: Presents an alternative vision but framed to the Green base.

rigor.statement: Luxon's short term sugar hits–selling out to overseas mining and oil gas companies while sidelining small businesses desperately seeking investment in productive, long-term economic development–treat our country like a quarry, not a world class economy.
rigor.explanation: Colourful characterisation without evidence linking the policies to the claimed harm.

veracity.statement: The HYEFU shows unemployment increasing next year–with everyday New Zealanders taking the hit.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with HYEFU projecting rising unemployment; a fair reading of the forecast.

veracity.statement: Willis' economic strategy has failed, and the cost is being paid by New Zealanders,
veracity.explanation: An evaluative verdict tied to real downward HYEFU revisions but 'failed' is a contestable judgement.

civility.statement: Luxon's short term sugar hits–selling out to overseas mining and oil gas companies while sidelining small businesses desperately seeking investment in productive, long-term economic development–treat our country like a quarry, not a world class economy.
civility.explanation: 'Selling out' and 'quarry' framing attacks the Government's motives rhetorically.

civility.statement: Willis' economic strategy has failed, and the cost is being paid by New Zealanders,
civility.explanation: Attacks the strategy and names the minister but stays on the policy record.

divination.statement: The HYEFU shows unemployment increasing next year–with everyday New Zealanders taking the hit.
divination.explanation: Relays an official forecast of rising unemployment; plausible but forecasts carry uncertainty.

specificity.statement: In 2022 NZ adopted the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and committed to protect at least 30% of the world's ocean by 2030.
specificity.explanation: Names the framework, year and the specific target and deadline.

specificity.statement: do the scientifically necessary actions to end bottom trawling in the Gulf and protect at least 30% of our oceans
specificity.explanation: Names concrete actions (end bottom trawling, 30% protection) but not how or when.

charisma.statement: The National Party went into the election promising accelerated protection in the Gulf. Passing this bill is a necessary step to achieve that.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to the incoming Government's own stated promise to find common ground.

rigor.statement: The National Party went into the election promising accelerated protection in the Gulf. Passing this bill is a necessary step to achieve that.
rigor.explanation: Ties the ask logically to the opponent's own commitment.

rigor.statement: do the scientifically necessary actions to end bottom trawling in the Gulf and protect at least 30% of our oceans
rigor.explanation: Frames the ask as evidence-led though the 'scientifically necessary' claim is asserted.

veracity.statement: The National Party went into the election promising accelerated protection in the Gulf. Passing this bill is a necessary step to achieve that.
veracity.explanation: National did campaign on Gulf protection; accurate reference to their commitment.

veracity.statement: In 2022 NZ adopted the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and committed to protect at least 30% of the world's ocean by 2030.
veracity.explanation: Accurate: NZ signed up to the Kunming-Montreal framework with the 30x30 target.

veracity.statement: The Hauraki Gulf/Tīkapa Moana/Te Moananui ā Toi ecosystem is on the brink of collapse.
veracity.explanation: State-of-the-Gulf reporting shows serious degradation; 'on the brink of collapse' overstates a real decline.

specificity.statement: Climate change is barely mentioned across this plan, and even then, it is to state that the Government will be initiating a review of its methane targets that excludes farming related methane, and that it will keep farming out of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS).
specificity.explanation: Cites specific policy contents of the plan.

rigor.statement: Christopher Luxon is not in the boardroom anymore.
rigor.explanation: Ad hominem framing with no argument.

rigor.statement: When someone shows you who they are, believe them. This Government has shown these past six months that its focus is squarely on gutting environmental, climate and social gains in order to line the pockets of a few at the top.
rigor.explanation: Motive attribution presented as proven without evidence.

rigor.statement: Climate change is barely mentioned across this plan, and even then, it is to state that the Government will be initiating a review of its methane targets that excludes farming related methane, and that it will keep farming out of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS).
rigor.explanation: Backs the criticism with concrete plan contents.

rigor.statement: this coalition of cowards is too scared to defy the demands of their donors and do what is right and fight for a liveable climate.
rigor.explanation: Ad hominem and imputed motive with no evidence.

rigor.statement: It is the same story with bootcamps which have failed in the past and will do the same in the future.
rigor.explanation: Extrapolates future failure from past record, a reasonable but unevidenced-here inference.

veracity.statement: Climate change is barely mentioned across this plan, and even then, it is to state that the Government will be initiating a review of its methane targets that excludes farming related methane, and that it will keep farming out of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS).
veracity.explanation: Accurately reflects the plan's methane review and keeping agriculture out of the ETS.

civility.statement: Christopher Luxon is not in the boardroom anymore.
civility.explanation: A personal jab at Luxon's background rather than engaging the policy.

civility.statement: When someone shows you who they are, believe them. This Government has shown these past six months that its focus is squarely on gutting environmental, climate and social gains in order to line the pockets of a few at the top.
civility.explanation: Imputes self-serving motives ('line the pockets of a few').

civility.statement: this coalition of cowards is too scared to defy the demands of their donors and do what is right and fight for a liveable climate.
civility.explanation: Name-calling ('coalition of cowards') and an unevidenced donor-corruption implication.

divination.statement: It is the same story with bootcamps which have failed in the past and will do the same in the future.
divination.explanation: Predicts bootcamps will fail again; past NZ boot-camp evaluations support the direction but outcomes vary.

specificity.statement: It is shameful that New Zealand has one of the highest imprisonment rates in the developed world.
specificity.explanation: General comparative claim, no figure given.

specificity.statement: If the Government genuinely cared about addressing people's concerns about crime then it could take action to address the causes of offending, including mental healthcare, addiction treatment, housing and liveable income support, while introducing a new pathway away from prisons.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete alternative interventions (mental health, addiction, housing, income support).

rigor.statement: Bringing back the failed three strikes law will lead to grossly unfair results that disproportionately impact Māori, including much harsher sentences than would otherwise be imposed,
rigor.explanation: Draws on the historical record of the earlier law.

rigor.statement: This is despite mounting evidence that mass incarceration has failed to bring down rates of crime, keep communities safe, or rehabilitate those in our system.
rigor.explanation: Appeals to a body of criminological evidence, though not cited specifically here.

rigor.statement: The Government is hell-bent on funnelling more and more people into prisons.
rigor.explanation: Asserts motive ('hell-bent') without evidence.

rigor.statement: If the Government genuinely cared about addressing people's concerns about crime then it could take action to address the causes of offending, including mental healthcare, addiction treatment, housing and liveable income support, while introducing a new pathway away from prisons.
rigor.explanation: Offers an evidence-oriented causes-of-crime argument, though 'if genuinely cared' is a rhetorical hook.

rigor.statement: The three strikes law means that mistakes that people might make as teenagers will be with them for their entire life.
rigor.explanation: Reasoned from how the law operates, though stated in emotive terms.

veracity.statement: Bringing back the failed three strikes law will lead to grossly unfair results that disproportionately impact Māori, including much harsher sentences than would otherwise be imposed,
veracity.explanation: The prior three strikes regime did disproportionately affect Māori, supporting the claim.

veracity.statement: It is shameful that New Zealand has one of the highest imprisonment rates in the developed world.
veracity.explanation: NZ's incarceration rate is indeed high among OECD countries.

veracity.statement: This is despite mounting evidence that mass incarceration has failed to bring down rates of crime, keep communities safe, or rehabilitate those in our system.
veracity.explanation: Reflects a substantial evidence base questioning incarceration's deterrent value, contested in parts.

civility.statement: The Government is hell-bent on funnelling more and more people into prisons.
civility.explanation: Charged characterisation of intent, aimed at policy direction.

civility.statement: If the Government genuinely cared about addressing people's concerns about crime then it could take action to address the causes of offending, including mental healthcare, addiction treatment, housing and liveable income support, while introducing a new pathway away from prisons.
civility.explanation: The 'if genuinely cared' framing questions the Government's sincerity.

divination.statement: Bringing back the failed three strikes law will lead to grossly unfair results that disproportionately impact Māori, including much harsher sentences than would otherwise be imposed,
divination.explanation: Predicts disproportionate Māori impact; consistent with the original regime's documented effects, though magnitude uncertain.

divination.statement: The three strikes law means that mistakes that people might make as teenagers will be with them for their entire life.
divination.explanation: Predicts lifelong consequences from the regime's mechanics; plausible given mandatory sentencing but generalised.

specificity.statement: Every family deserves to live with dignity, no household should be forced to go into debt to survive
specificity.explanation: A values platitude with no mechanism, figure, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: A Green Government will regulate debt collectors and lift income levels above the poverty line so that families aren’t drowning in debt and can live in dignity
specificity.explanation: Names two concrete actions (regulate collectors, lift incomes above poverty line) but no figures or timeframe.

civility.statement: Every family deserves to live with dignity, no household should be forced to go into debt to survive
civility.explanation: Respectful, issue-focused, no personal attack.

civility.statement: Instead of supporting people in need, Christopher Luxon has dished out billions of dollars worth of tax cuts to landlords and tobacco companies.
civility.explanation: Pointed policy criticism naming the PM, edging into loaded 'dished out' framing but not a personal attack.

charisma.statement: Every family deserves to live with dignity, no household should be forced to go into debt to survive
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, dignity-focused framing, but appeals to sympathetic audience only.

veracity.statement: Instead of supporting people in need, Christopher Luxon has dished out billions of dollars worth of tax cuts to landlords and tobacco companies.
veracity.explanation: Interest-deductibility restoration for landlords (~$2.9b) is real, but 'billions to tobacco companies' overstates the excise/regulatory changes; framing is misleading on magnitude.

veracity.statement: We know more families are being declined for assistance at Work and Income, which is leading them right into the hands of loan sharks.
veracity.explanation: Declined-assistance trend is plausible but unquantified; the causal 'leading them into loan sharks' is asserted, not evidenced.

rigor.statement: Instead of supporting people in need, Christopher Luxon has dished out billions of dollars worth of tax cuts to landlords and tobacco companies.
rigor.explanation: Rhetorical juxtaposition (help-the-needy vs tax-cuts-for-landlords) without quantified backing; leans on emotive framing.

rigor.statement: We know more families are being declined for assistance at Work and Income, which is leading them right into the hands of loan sharks.
rigor.explanation: Asserts a causal chain from declines to predatory lending without supporting data.

strength.statement: A Green Government will regulate debt collectors and lift income levels above the poverty line so that families aren’t drowning in debt and can live in dignity
strength.explanation: Opposition commitment with no delivery mechanism or means to enact it from outside government.

specificity.statement: Tax rebates for childcare will be nothing more than a drop in the ocean for families struggling to get by
specificity.explanation: Metaphor ('drop in the ocean'), no figures on rebate size or shortfall.

specificity.statement: A Government serious about the well-being of children would not be reducing the benefits and incomes of our most vulnerable families. It would not be threatening public housing tenants and their children with homelessness. It would not be cutting school lunches. And it certainly would not be doing all of this to fund tax cuts for the rich.
specificity.explanation: References several concrete policies (benefits, public housing, school lunches, tax cuts) though without figures.

specificity.statement: Making childcare more affordable for families requires more than mere tax cuts. It demands action across a range of areas - from investing in community early childhood education, pay equity for teachers, ensuring all kids have access to quality care options, and working towards universal, public, free early childhood education.
specificity.explanation: Names several policy directions (community ECE investment, pay equity, universal free ECE) but no costings or timeline.

civility.statement: Once again, National is demonstrating that they're not actually interested in supporting people.
civility.explanation: Attacks motives/character of the party rather than engaging the policy substance.

civility.statement: A Government serious about the well-being of children would not be reducing the benefits and incomes of our most vulnerable families. It would not be threatening public housing tenants and their children with homelessness. It would not be cutting school lunches. And it certainly would not be doing all of this to fund tax cuts for the rich.
civility.explanation: Frames opponents as unserious about children; accumulates charges rhetorically rather than engaging counter-arguments.

charisma.statement: Making childcare more affordable for families requires more than mere tax cuts. It demands action across a range of areas - from investing in community early childhood education, pay equity for teachers, ensuring all kids have access to quality care options, and working towards universal, public, free early childhood education.
charisma.explanation: Constructive, solutions-oriented tone but aimed at its own base.

veracity.statement: Over the last twenty years, more and more community-based early childhood centres have closed and large, for-profit chains have expanded.
veracity.explanation: Broadly consistent with the growth of large private ECE providers, though 'more and more closed' is unquantified and partly contested.

rigor.statement: Once again, National is demonstrating that they're not actually interested in supporting people.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping motive attribution ('not interested in supporting people') from a single policy — hasty generalization.

rigor.statement: A Government serious about the well-being of children would not be reducing the benefits and incomes of our most vulnerable families. It would not be threatening public housing tenants and their children with homelessness. It would not be cutting school lunches. And it certainly would not be doing all of this to fund tax cuts for the rich.
rigor.explanation: Lists real policy changes but strings them into a motive claim ('to fund tax cuts for the rich') without demonstrating the fiscal link.

divination.statement: Tax rebates for childcare will be nothing more than a drop in the ocean for families struggling to get by
divination.explanation: Predicts the rebate's impact will be negligible; directionally plausible for modest rebates but magnitude unverified.

specificity.statement: Rangatahi deserve more than child prisons and military bootcamps. They deserve opportunities
specificity.explanation: Value framing with loaded labels; no concrete alternative programme specified here.

specificity.statement: When the Office of the Children’s Commissioner reported on Korowai Manaaki recently, they revealed inappropriate and deeply troubling practices within the residences.
specificity.explanation: Names the facility and source but not the specific practices.

civility.statement: Rangatahi deserve more than child prisons and military bootcamps. They deserve opportunities
civility.explanation: Criticises policies using charged terms ('child prisons') but not personal attacks.

civility.statement: Unfortunately, this culture can be seen across the youth justice space in Aotearoa and is a product of politicians who put winning votes above the real needs of children.
civility.explanation: Attributes bad faith ('winning votes above the real needs of children') to politicians generally.

veracity.statement: I have visited these youth justice residences and can confirm that they are child prisons.
veracity.explanation: The secure-residence conditions are real, but 'child prisons' is a rhetorical characterisation rather than a factual designation.

veracity.statement: Years of research and experience shows that youth justice residences are re-traumatising and ineffective.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with substantial research on youth incarceration harms, but stated as unqualified fact.

veracity.statement: When the Office of the Children’s Commissioner reported on Korowai Manaaki recently, they revealed inappropriate and deeply troubling practices within the residences.
veracity.explanation: Refers to a specific oversight report; critical monitoring findings on OT residences are well documented.

rigor.statement: Years of research and experience shows that youth justice residences are re-traumatising and ineffective.
rigor.explanation: Appeals to a body of research without citing it, though the direction aligns with much criminological evidence.

rigor.statement: Unfortunately, this culture can be seen across the youth justice space in Aotearoa and is a product of politicians who put winning votes above the real needs of children.
rigor.explanation: Motive attribution and generalisation across the whole sector without supporting evidence.

authenticity.statement: I have visited these youth justice residences and can confirm that they are child prisons.
authenticity.explanation: Bases the claim on first-hand visits, consistent with the party's stated position; the 'child prisons' label is her characterisation.

specificity.statement: Everyone deserves to feel safe in sport, including our trans whānau
specificity.explanation: General principle, no mechanism.

civility.statement: It is abundantly clear that this is a political move to appease coalition partners and appeal to some of the most hate-filled corners of our society.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad motive and associates the decision with 'hate-filled' groups rather than engaging the rationale.

civility.statement: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has failed transgender, takatāpui and rainbow communities yet again.
civility.explanation: Personalised blame on the PM; a sweeping 'failed yet again' judgement rather than substantive critique.

charisma.statement: Everyone deserves to feel safe in sport, including our trans whānau
charisma.explanation: Inclusive 'everyone' framing that invites broad agreement.

veracity.statement: Minister Mark Mitchell said himself that there was nothing wrong with the guidelines.
veracity.explanation: Reports a specific attributed statement by the Minister; plausible but not independently verifiable from the text.

rigor.statement: It is abundantly clear that this is a political move to appease coalition partners and appeal to some of the most hate-filled corners of our society.
rigor.explanation: Motive assertion ('abundantly clear') presented as self-evident without evidence.

specificity.statement: The Government is now looking at a $5 billion bill materialising by 2030.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar figure and date.

specificity.statement: Climate commitments are baked into our free trade agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union. If Luxon walks away from that 2030 target, he puts our trading relationships and exporters' market access on the line too.
specificity.explanation: Names specific agreements and the 2030 target.

civility.statement: If the Greens dared to pretend we would do something without budgeting for it, these guys would be screeching bloody murder. The economic incompetence and double standards here is unreal.
civility.explanation: 'Screeching bloody murder' and 'economic incompetence' are dismissive/hyperbolic rather than substantive.

veracity.statement: Every time Christopher Luxon has cut climate action here at home, he has increased the bill we need to pay other countries to reduce their emissions
veracity.explanation: Directionally accurate on the onshore/offshore trade-off, though causal attribution to the PM is simplified.

veracity.statement: We have known for about a decade doing that will require offshore mitigation, but the size of that offshore cost depends on how much we do onshore.
veracity.explanation: Accurate: NZ's NDC has long been understood to require offshore mitigation, scaled by domestic effort.

veracity.statement: The Government is now looking at a $5 billion bill materialising by 2030.
veracity.explanation: Cites Treasury's figure, though presenting the upper-bound 'up to $5b' as 'a $5 billion bill' loses that caveat.

veracity.statement: Climate commitments are baked into our free trade agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union. If Luxon walks away from that 2030 target, he puts our trading relationships and exporters' market access on the line too.
veracity.explanation: NZ's FTAs with the EU/UK do contain climate/sustainability commitments; the trade-access risk is asserted more strongly than the treaty text guarantees.

rigor.statement: Every time Christopher Luxon has cut climate action here at home, he has increased the bill we need to pay other countries to reduce their emissions
rigor.explanation: Sound underlying logic (less domestic mitigation → more offshore purchase) but 'every time' overstates as an absolute rule.

rigor.statement: We have known for about a decade doing that will require offshore mitigation, but the size of that offshore cost depends on how much we do onshore.
rigor.explanation: Clear premise-to-conclusion reasoning about the onshore-offshore relationship.

rigor.statement: If the Greens dared to pretend we would do something without budgeting for it, these guys would be screeching bloody murder. The economic incompetence and double standards here is unreal.
rigor.explanation: Hypothetical double-standard framing; asserts incompetence without demonstrating it.

rigor.statement: Climate commitments are baked into our free trade agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union. If Luxon walks away from that 2030 target, he puts our trading relationships and exporters' market access on the line too.
rigor.explanation: Reasonable if-then structure resting on the FTA-linkage premise.

rigor.statement: All politics aside, these are immutable facts.
rigor.explanation: Asserting 'immutable facts' about contingent projections overstates certainty; rhetorical closing rather than argument.

divination.statement: The Government is now looking at a $5 billion bill materialising by 2030.
divination.explanation: Prediction to 2030 grounded in Treasury's 'up to $5b' analysis; plausible but dependent on future policy and credit prices.

divination.statement: Climate commitments are baked into our free trade agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union. If Luxon walks away from that 2030 target, he puts our trading relationships and exporters' market access on the line too.
divination.explanation: Conditional prediction that abandoning the target risks market access; plausible but uncertain.

specificity.statement: Te Tiriti o Waitangi is something that binds us together in building a future for all of us, it is not something that should be used to drive us apart.
specificity.explanation: Aspirational, no concrete measure.

specificity.statement: From the Treaty Principles Bill and undermining marine customary title, to the removal of 7AA from the Oranga Tamariki Act and now this, the assaults and insults to our founding agreement and our people have been relentless from this Government.
specificity.explanation: Names several specific policies (Treaty Principles Bill, marine customary title, 7AA repeal).

civility.statement: This attack on the tribunal is nothing more than an attempt to limit the accountability the Government has to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
civility.explanation: 'Attack' framing and motive imputation rather than engaging the review's stated rationale.

civility.statement: From the Treaty Principles Bill and undermining marine customary title, to the removal of 7AA from the Oranga Tamariki Act and now this, the assaults and insults to our founding agreement and our people have been relentless from this Government.
civility.explanation: 'Assaults and insults... relentless' is charged characterisation of intent rather than measured critique.

charisma.statement: Te Tiriti o Waitangi is something that binds us together in building a future for all of us, it is not something that should be used to drive us apart.
charisma.explanation: Unifying 'binds us together... for all of us' framing that reaches beyond one group.

veracity.statement: Across this term, we have seen the actions of this Government trigger a record amount of urgent claims with the Waitangi Tribunal.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with the reported surge in urgent Waitangi Tribunal inquiries during this term, though 'record' is asserted.

rigor.statement: This attack on the tribunal is nothing more than an attempt to limit the accountability the Government has to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
rigor.explanation: Asserts the government's true motive ('nothing more than') without evidence.

specificity.statement: The Government’s trickle-down tax cuts come at unfathomable cost to people and planet
specificity.explanation: 'Unfathomable cost' is vague, no figures.

specificity.statement: 64 per cent of the benefit goes to the top 40 per cent of households. Just 5.2 per cent will flow to the lowest-income 20 per cent of New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Precise percentages tied to defined income groups.

charisma.statement: As someone who wears his police service medal with pride, I can understand the significance of Apiata's selfless act. Labour stands ready to work with the Minister for Veterans and all parties to reform the veterans' qualifying system.

veracity.statement: The Prime Minister said he would march in the street against modern slavery and yet 18 months into Government, he has failed to take any meaningful action or show any leadership,

authenticity.statement: Christopher Luxon promised to reduce the number of people on Jobseeker by 50,000, instead nearly 30,000 more Kiwis are now relying on it.
authenticity.explanation: Highlights the gap between Luxon's stated target and results — a low-authenticity signal about Luxon per the rubric.

civility.statement: This is a government that can't be trusted. They consistently punch down when it comes to beneficiaries, and stigmatise those that are out of work, yet their policies have made more people unemployed
civility.explanation: 'Can't be trusted' and 'punch down' are accusatory characterisations, though the unemployment point is substantive.

civility.statement: Today we see numbers which confirm what we already felt in Aotearoa – the Government is taking Māori backwards in every way possible
civility.explanation: 'Backwards in every way possible' is sweeping and combative.

civility.statement: It appears after nine months that this lazy Government has no plan to help Māori people who are out of work get jobs either.
civility.explanation: 'Lazy Government' is a derogatory characterisation rather than substantive critique.

civility.statement: Government has given nothing but crumbs to Māori, and these numbers will continue to grow as a result
civility.explanation: 'Nothing but crumbs' is dismissive rhetoric aimed at the Government's record.

specificity.statement: It appears after nine months that this lazy Government has no plan to help Māori people who are out of work get jobs either.
specificity.explanation: Asserts 'no plan' with no concrete detail.

rigor.statement: This is a government that can't be trusted. They consistently punch down when it comes to beneficiaries, and stigmatise those that are out of work, yet their policies have made more people unemployed
rigor.explanation: Asserts government policies caused rising unemployment without isolating cause from wider economic conditions.

veracity.statement: Under our Government we saw record levels of low unemployment for Pacific and now we have more out of work.
veracity.explanation: Pacific unemployment did reach historic lows under Labour amid overall record-low unemployment; broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: Today we see numbers which confirm what we already felt in Aotearoa – the Government is taking Māori backwards in every way possible
veracity.explanation: 'In every way possible' is hyperbole that overstates what the unemployment data alone show.

authenticity.statement: Under our Government we saw record levels of low unemployment for Pacific and now we have more out of work.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with Labour's record during a period of very low unemployment.

divination.statement: Government has given nothing but crumbs to Māori, and these numbers will continue to grow as a result
divination.explanation: Predicts Māori unemployment numbers will keep rising; directionally plausible but unquantified.

civility.statement: They are running the school lunch programme into the ground, meaning more children aren't getting the hot, healthy meal that was sometimes their only one in the day.
civility.explanation: Harsh characterisation of a programme's delivery, focused on policy outcomes.

civility.statement: I'm worried about children in this country, who seem to be becoming more and more of an afterthought by the day
civility.explanation: Expresses concern rather than attacking a person; mildly rhetorical.

specificity.statement: The Government has reversed the measure Labour put in place to ensure benefits rise with the average wage – which the Children's Commissioner said at the time was the single best thing a government could do to lift children out of poverty.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific policy (wage-indexation of benefits) and cites the Children's Commissioner.

specificity.statement: They cut public services for measly tax cuts, which have been more than offset by their decisions to cut free prescriptions, cut free and half-price public transport, and introduced a rebate scheme for childcare that isn't delivering what was promised.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates several concrete policy changes.

specificity.statement: Just this week, Nicola Willis wouldn't commit to not cutting the best start payment, which helps out new parents and the winter energy payment which helps families heat their homes in winter.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific payments and the minister and a rough timeframe.

specificity.statement: I'm worried about children in this country, who seem to be becoming more and more of an afterthought by the day
specificity.explanation: Emotional expression of concern with no concrete content.

rigor.statement: The Government has reversed the measure Labour put in place to ensure benefits rise with the average wage – which the Children's Commissioner said at the time was the single best thing a government could do to lift children out of poverty.
rigor.explanation: Uses the Commissioner's authority to support the point; reasonable but leans on an appeal to authority.

veracity.statement: The Government has reversed the measure Labour put in place to ensure benefits rise with the average wage – which the Children's Commissioner said at the time was the single best thing a government could do to lift children out of poverty.
veracity.explanation: The Government did change benefit indexation from wages back to inflation (CPI); accurately described.

veracity.statement: They are running the school lunch programme into the ground, meaning more children aren't getting the hot, healthy meal that was sometimes their only one in the day.
veracity.explanation: The revamped school lunch programme faced widely reported delivery problems; 'into the ground' is hyperbolic framing of a real issue.

veracity.statement: They cut public services for measly tax cuts, which have been more than offset by their decisions to cut free prescriptions, cut free and half-price public transport, and introduced a rebate scheme for childcare that isn't delivering what was promised.
veracity.explanation: The reinstated $5 prescription co-pay and removal of half-price public transport are real; the 'more than offset' claim is a contestable aggregate assertion.

veracity.statement: Just this week, Nicola Willis wouldn't commit to not cutting the best start payment, which helps out new parents and the winter energy payment which helps families heat their homes in winter.
veracity.explanation: Reports a non-commitment by Willis; the underlying event is plausible but 'wouldn't commit' framing is characterisation.

charisma.statement: Where it is safe to do so, we do not oppose raising speed limits. However, the Government's making many of these changes based on a campaign promise, rather than evidence
charisma.explanation: Acknowledges common ground (supports higher limits where safe) before disagreeing — a measured, bridge-acknowledging stance.

civility.statement: Where it is safe to do so, we do not oppose raising speed limits. However, the Government's making many of these changes based on a campaign promise, rather than evidence
civility.explanation: Concedes the opponent's aim can be legitimate and critiques the basis of the decision, not the person.

civility.statement: We know this, because the previous Transport Minister encouraged National Party supporters to submit on his own bill. He was not interested in the opposing views of safety campaigners.
civility.explanation: Criticises the minister's process conduct rather than launching a personal insult.

civility.statement: Any road deaths as a result of increased speed limits will now be on the Government's hands.
civility.explanation: Assigns blame for future deaths pre-emptively — an emotive, accusatory framing.

civility.statement: I do remain concerned about the potential for more deaths on the roads as a result of these changes
civility.explanation: Expressed as a measured concern rather than an accusation.

rigor.statement: Where it is safe to do so, we do not oppose raising speed limits. However, the Government's making many of these changes based on a campaign promise, rather than evidence
rigor.explanation: Draws a clear distinction between evidence-based and campaign-driven policy; reasoned though the evidence claim is asserted.

rigor.statement: We know this, because the previous Transport Minister encouraged National Party supporters to submit on his own bill. He was not interested in the opposing views of safety campaigners.
rigor.explanation: Offers a supporting reason (partisan submissions push) for the 'not evidence-based' claim, but the inference about disinterest is characterisation.

divination.statement: Any road deaths as a result of increased speed limits will now be on the Government's hands.
divination.explanation: Implies increased limits will cause deaths; evidence links higher speeds to greater harm, but attribution of specific deaths is uncertain.

divination.statement: I do remain concerned about the potential for more deaths on the roads as a result of these changes
divination.explanation: A hedged prediction of more road deaths from higher speeds; supported in direction by road-safety evidence but unquantified.

civility.statement: Nicola Willis has had almost two years, yet she is still dithering over options to improve competition in the grocery sector. A fast-track regime for supermarkets makes sense, but it won't make any immediate difference for New Zealanders who will keep paying high prices at the checkout today
civility.explanation: 'Dithering' is a pointed jab at the Minister, but the substance engages a real policy question and even concedes the fast-track 'makes sense'.

civility.statement: Soundbites don't put food on the table, shoes on feet or petrol in cars. New Zealanders are tired of hearing the same old phrase from the Government – that things are tough – with little action to help.
civility.explanation: Criticises the Government's communication rather than a person, but is dismissive rhetoric ('soundbites').

civility.statement: National talked a big game on cost of living and haven't delivered. They have no idea what most people and small businesses are really going through and no plan to turn things around
civility.explanation: 'No idea what people are going through' is a personal/character attack rather than a policy critique.

specificity.statement: Nicola Willis has had almost two years, yet she is still dithering over options to improve competition in the grocery sector. A fast-track regime for supermarkets makes sense, but it won't make any immediate difference for New Zealanders who will keep paying high prices at the checkout today
specificity.explanation: Names the policy area and timeframe ('almost two years') but offers no concrete alternative mechanism or figures.

specificity.statement: Soundbites don't put food on the table, shoes on feet or petrol in cars. New Zealanders are tired of hearing the same old phrase from the Government – that things are tough – with little action to help.
specificity.explanation: Rhetorical framing with no mechanism, figure or concrete claim.

specificity.statement: Kiwis still won't see their grocery bills coming down for years under National.
specificity.explanation: Vague timeframe ('for years') with no mechanism.

specificity.statement: National talked a big game on cost of living and haven't delivered. They have no idea what most people and small businesses are really going through and no plan to turn things around
specificity.explanation: Sweeping assertion with no supporting detail.

divination.statement: Nicola Willis has had almost two years, yet she is still dithering over options to improve competition in the grocery sector. A fast-track regime for supermarkets makes sense, but it won't make any immediate difference for New Zealanders who will keep paying high prices at the checkout today
divination.explanation: Predicts a fast-track regime won't ease prices immediately; plausible given supply-side reforms take time to affect retail prices.

divination.statement: Kiwis still won't see their grocery bills coming down for years under National.
divination.explanation: Prediction that grocery prices won't fall for years; directionally plausible as grocery inflation is sticky, but 'years' is an unquantified worst-case.

charisma.statement: Nicola Willis has had almost two years, yet she is still dithering over options to improve competition in the grocery sector. A fast-track regime for supermarkets makes sense, but it won't make any immediate difference for New Zealanders who will keep paying high prices at the checkout today
charisma.explanation: Concedes a point to the opponent ('makes sense') but overall is a partisan critique appealing to its own side.

authenticity.statement: Labour was serious about more competition in the grocery sector and laid the groundwork for this.
authenticity.explanation: Labour did commission a Commerce Commission market study and pass the Grocery Industry Competition Act, so the claim is broadly consistent with its record, though 'serious'/'laid the groundwork' overstates limited results.

strength.statement: Labour was serious about more competition in the grocery sector and laid the groundwork for this.
strength.explanation: Points to real groundwork (market study, grocery commissioner) but delivery of actual new competition was not achieved in office.

civility.statement: All while the cost of living continues to go up and the country goes backwards,
civility.explanation: General critique of conditions, no personal attack.

civility.statement: The National Party did this last time. Public houses got so run down that a big investment was needed to do them up, and instead of fronting up what was needed they sold the houses off instead.
civility.explanation: Critiques party record and policy rather than personal character.

civility.statement: To also take $40 million from Māori Housing providers and $20 million out of transitional housing for rangatahi youth – there's no regard here for Kiwis who need a hand, but plenty for those who don't,
civility.explanation: Imputes callousness ('no regard') to the Government rather than debating the merits.

specificity.statement: Christopher Luxon and Nicola Willis promised big tax cuts of $250 a fortnight, said they'd fund a specific 13 cancer drugs and that they would provide cost of living relief. They campaigned on these things and asked for people to vote for them.
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete figures ($250 a fortnight, 13 drugs) and named commitments.

specificity.statement: Instead, they're giving billions to landlords and more people are losing money from the tax changes than getting the amount promised. Pensioners are only getting $2.50.
specificity.explanation: Gives concrete figures ($2.50, billions) though the derivations are unstated.

specificity.statement: All while the cost of living continues to go up and the country goes backwards,
specificity.explanation: Vague slogan ('country goes backwards') with no metric.

specificity.statement: Instead, there is $1.5 billion less for building and maintaining public houses, which will slow the progress we've made as a country to fix the housing crisis. The Government has cut $435 million from the Kāinga Ora house build programme and over $1 billion from the maintenance fund.
specificity.explanation: Breaks the $1.5b down into $435m build and $1b+ maintenance components.

specificity.statement: Residential investment over the year to December 2024 is forecast to be nearly 11% lower than in 2023.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure (nearly 11%) and timeframe.

specificity.statement: To also take $40 million from Māori Housing providers and $20 million out of transitional housing for rangatahi youth – there's no regard here for Kiwis who need a hand, but plenty for those who don't,
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures ($40m, $20m) for named programmes, though the 'those who don't' is vague.

divination.statement: Instead, there is $1.5 billion less for building and maintaining public houses, which will slow the progress we've made as a country to fix the housing crisis. The Government has cut $435 million from the Kāinga Ora house build programme and over $1 billion from the maintenance fund.
divination.explanation: Predicts the reductions 'will slow' housing progress; plausible but unquantified.

divination.statement: Residential investment over the year to December 2024 is forecast to be nearly 11% lower than in 2023.
divination.explanation: A forecast of an ~11% fall in residential investment; consistent with then-current downturn expectations.

veracity.statement: Christopher Luxon and Nicola Willis promised big tax cuts of $250 a fortnight, said they'd fund a specific 13 cancer drugs and that they would provide cost of living relief. They campaigned on these things and asked for people to vote for them.
veracity.explanation: Largely accurate: National campaigned on '$250 a fortnight' for some households and 13 cancer drugs, though $250 was a max for a specific household type, not a universal figure.

veracity.statement: Instead, they're giving billions to landlords and more people are losing money from the tax changes than getting the amount promised. Pensioners are only getting $2.50.
veracity.explanation: '$2.50 for pensioners' and 'billions to landlords' (interest deductibility) reference real policies but the framing selectively presents worst cases and is contestable.

veracity.statement: Instead, there is $1.5 billion less for building and maintaining public houses, which will slow the progress we've made as a country to fix the housing crisis. The Government has cut $435 million from the Kāinga Ora house build programme and over $1 billion from the maintenance fund.
veracity.explanation: Figures broadly track Budget 2024 reprioritisations of Kāinga Ora funding, though 'cut' is contested framing of reduced future increases.

veracity.statement: The National Party did this last time. Public houses got so run down that a big investment was needed to do them up, and instead of fronting up what was needed they sold the houses off instead.
veracity.explanation: National did sell state houses and reduce stock in its 2008-17 term, broadly supporting the historical claim.

veracity.statement: Residential investment over the year to December 2024 is forecast to be nearly 11% lower than in 2023.
veracity.explanation: A specific forecast figure consistent with Treasury/Budget forecasts of a construction downturn, though attribution to Government policy is contestable.

rigor.statement: The National Party did this last time. Public houses got so run down that a big investment was needed to do them up, and instead of fronting up what was needed they sold the houses off instead.
rigor.explanation: Draws on historical precedent to argue a pattern, but relies on analogy to the previous government rather than direct evidence for the current case.

civility.statement: The lack of any action from the Government to bring down unemployment for hard-working Pacific people is shameful,
civility.explanation: 'Shameful' is a value judgment on the Government's inaction rather than a personal insult, but is emotive.

civility.statement: It's disheartening to see more Pacific people unemployed as the Government chooses to cut public service jobs and scrap housing and infrastructure projects, while giving billions to landlords and the tobacco lobby.
civility.explanation: 'Tobacco lobby' framing is loaded, but criticises policy choices rather than character.

civility.statement: Nicola Willis' slash-and-burn Budget is promising even more pain for communities. Pacific people deserve so much more than the hogwash they've gotten so far from National.
civility.explanation: 'Slash-and-burn' and 'hogwash' are dismissive, sensationalist rhetoric rather than substantive critique.

specificity.statement: The lack of any action from the Government to bring down unemployment for hard-working Pacific people is shameful,
specificity.explanation: No specific measure or figure within the statement.

specificity.statement: It's disheartening to see more Pacific people unemployed as the Government chooses to cut public service jobs and scrap housing and infrastructure projects, while giving billions to landlords and the tobacco lobby.
specificity.explanation: Lists specific policy areas but no figures or mechanisms.

specificity.statement: Nicola Willis' slash-and-burn Budget is promising even more pain for communities. Pacific people deserve so much more than the hogwash they've gotten so far from National.

rigor.statement: It's disheartening to see more Pacific people unemployed as the Government chooses to cut public service jobs and scrap housing and infrastructure projects, while giving billions to landlords and the tobacco lobby.

civility.statement: It doesn't create a single new bed, it doesn't provide support, and it doesn't deliver a permanent roof over someone's head. It just shifts the problem from the CBD to people's neighbourhoods,
civility.explanation: Attacks the policy's effect, not a person.

civility.statement: Moving someone from one doorstep to the next does not fix homelessness. 'Move‑on' powers don't build homes or connect people with support,
civility.explanation: Engages the substance of the policy without personal attack.

civility.statement: Slapping fines or threatening prison time on those who can't afford a safe place to sleep or something to eat is disgraceful.
civility.explanation: 'Disgraceful' is emotive, but aimed at the policy's effect on vulnerable people.

civility.statement: This is the National Government showing how little they care about Aucklanders who need support. They've cut support to social services and access to emergency accommodation, and failed to get people into homes, making things worse for those already needing help.
civility.explanation: 'How little they care' imputes motive/character rather than debating policy.

specificity.statement: Slapping fines or threatening prison time on those who can't afford a safe place to sleep or something to eat is disgraceful.
specificity.explanation: References fines/prison as consequences but no detail on the policy mechanism.

specificity.statement: Real solutions mean more homes people can actually live in, mental health and addiction support, opportunities to work and practical pathways off the street. That's how you reduce rough sleeping and keep people safe - not by moving it along to another suburb. Out of sight is not out of mind,
specificity.explanation: Names solution categories (housing, mental health support, work pathways) but no mechanisms, funding or targets.

charisma.statement: Real solutions mean more homes people can actually live in, mental health and addiction support, opportunities to work and practical pathways off the street. That's how you reduce rough sleeping and keep people safe - not by moving it along to another suburb. Out of sight is not out of mind,
charisma.explanation: Constructive, solutions-focused tone but still framed against the Government.

rigor.statement: It doesn't create a single new bed, it doesn't provide support, and it doesn't deliver a permanent roof over someone's head. It just shifts the problem from the CBD to people's neighbourhoods,

That's how you reduce rough sleeping and keep people safe - not by moving it along to another suburb. Out of sight is not out of mind,

civility.statement: Labour welcomes the Government's contribution of $2 million to earthquake relief efforts but it is imperative there is international pressure on the junta to stop its military action,

specificity.statement: Labour welcomes the Government's contribution of $2 million to earthquake relief efforts but it is imperative there is international pressure on the junta to stop its military action,
specificity.explanation: Cites the $2m figure and a clear ask (international pressure) but the ask itself is general.

specificity.statement: The junta needs to lift its curfew to allow aid workers to search for the missing, and end its ban on overseas journalists entering the country.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete demands: lift the curfew, end the journalist ban.

specificity.statement: The Myanmar military has a long track record of weaponizing humanitarian aid. Countries like New Zealand need to contribute to the relief effort but must also raise their voices to demand an end to the regime's war on its people, and strict humanitarian neutrality so that the people who need aid the most get it,
specificity.explanation: Calls for contribution, advocacy and humanitarian neutrality but without specific mechanisms or amounts.

charisma.statement: Labour welcomes the Government's contribution of $2 million to earthquake relief efforts but it is imperative there is international pressure on the junta to stop its military action,
charisma.explanation: Explicitly credits the Government's contribution before pressing further; bipartisan, consensus-building tone on a foreign-affairs issue.

veracity.statement: This is a regime that is at war with its own people. Since the earthquake they have continued to carry out airstrikes on townships.

rigor.statement: The Myanmar military has a long track record of weaponizing humanitarian aid. Countries like New Zealand need to contribute to the relief effort but must also raise their voices to demand an end to the regime's war on its people, and strict humanitarian neutrality so that the people who need aid the most get it,
rigor.explanation: Grounds its recommendation in the regime's documented track record; reasonable inference though the 'track record' is asserted rather than cited.

civility.statement: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and Police Minister Mark Mitchell are allocating police they haven't even managed to hire yet,

civility.statement: Cabinet has also agreed to transfer the power to make changes to our firearms laws – including what is defined as a prohibited weapon – to a gun lobbyist.
civility.explanation: 'Gun lobbyist' is a pejorative label rather than a neutral description.

specificity.statement: This means they're needing to hire another 604 police officers in order to increase the number of police by 500.
specificity.explanation: Precise derived figure (604).

veracity.statement: The actual number of police as at 26 August 2024 was 10,107. Their baseline figure from 27 November 2023 is 10,211 – that's a decrease of 104 police.

rigor.explanation: Uses named data (victimisation time-and-place) and target-vs-outcome figures to build the argument.

civility.statement: The Prime Minister wants to make houses more expensive for Kiwis and is hellbent on bringing foreign buyers back to buy up housing stock to push prices up even further.

veracity.statement: Christopher Luxon also insists his government has built thousands of public houses when his colleague Chris Bishop says they have only built 45.
veracity.explanation: Highlights a genuine apparent contradiction between ministers, but juxtaposes figures on different bases (total stock vs a specific new-build count) which is somewhat misleading.

civility.statement: National's been talking up our Defence spending like they're putting more money and resource in, but as we've seen time and time again with Christopher Luxon's Government, that rhetoric doesn't match reality.

specificity.statement: What this Government says and does are two entirely different things.

specificity.statement: My Members’ Bill on Online Safety reflects the report’s direction. It would put three clear legal duties on online service providers to ensure their platforms are safer.
specificity.explanation: References a specific bill and 'three clear legal duties', though the duties themselves are not enumerated here.

specificity.statement: We also need clear rules to control deepfake technology and a ban on “nudify” apps, which pose real risks to young people’s privacy and safety.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete measures (deepfake rules, banning 'nudify' apps) though without drafting detail.

strength.statement: My Members’ Bill on Online Safety reflects the report’s direction. It would put three clear legal duties on online service providers to ensure their platforms are safer.
