specificity.statement: We are spreading the word that fixing the basics and building the future is in the best interests of all NZers !
specificity.explanation: Party slogan with no concrete policy, figure or mechanism.

strength.statement: Thanks to the Government's careful management of the country's finances, new funding is able to be invested in hospitals, schools, roads, rail, defence capability, social housing and local infrastructure
strength.explanation: Claims investment across many areas but is a Budget announcement framing; delivery is stated rather than demonstrated.

strength.statement: We have made $50 billion of savings across three Budgets, and this year have redirected investment to new roads to help boost economic growth, to Police to crack down on crime, to schools so our kids are taught the basics brilliantly, and to the health system to ensure people get care when they need it.
strength.explanation: Claims delivered savings and redirected spending; partial delivery across Budgets but figures are contested.

strength.statement: Stalkers will face the full force of the law now that stalking has become a criminal offence punishable by up to five years in prison.
strength.explanation: Points to an enacted law rather than a mere promise, indicating follow-through.

strength.statement: We're also replacing NCEA with a credible, internationally benchmarked qualification – the New Zealand Certificate of Education at Year 12, and the New Zealand Advanced Certificate of Education at Year 13.
strength.explanation: A major announced reform, but replacing NCEA is a stated future intent with delivery still ahead.

strength.statement: Budget 2026 is delivering the next step towards a modern Tauranga Hospital, so families across our region can feel confident they'll get the care they need.
strength.explanation: Frames a Budget allocation as delivery, but this is an announced step rather than a completed project.

strength.statement: Broken glass has no place near a school or footpath.
strength.explanation: Accompanies a resolved constituent issue — he contacted the council and the cleanup was scheduled and confirmed — showing follow-through at local level.

charisma.statement: Thanks to the Government's careful management of the country's finances, new funding is able to be invested in hospitals, schools, roads, rail, defence capability, social housing and local infrastructure
charisma.explanation: Confident credit-claiming that appeals to supporters; no cross-party or consensus-seeking element.

charisma.statement: This will be free, because older New Zealanders should not have to pay just to prove who they are.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to a shared value (dignity of seniors) in an inclusive, unobjectionable way.

charisma.statement: If you see issues like this in our community, please don't hesitate to let me know. I'm here to help get them fixed.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, service-oriented invitation to constituents; approachable but routine.

charisma.statement: We are spreading the word that fixing the basics and building the future is in the best interests of all NZers !
charisma.explanation: Positive and inclusive in tone but purely a promotional talking point.

rigor.statement: The earlier return to surplus forecast in this year's Budget shows the benefits of disciplined economic management and a government taking its responsibilities seriously
rigor.explanation: Attributes an earlier surplus forecast to its own 'disciplined' management without isolating other drivers; leans on self-praise rather than evidence.

rigor.statement: New Zealand cannot tax, borrow and spend its way out of every challenge.
rigor.explanation: A rhetorical maxim with a false-dichotomy flavour; asserts rather than evidences the limits of fiscal expansion.

rigor.statement: Without a responsible path back to surplus, Kiwis would face the real risk of higher debt, higher interest rates and higher taxes.
rigor.explanation: Plausible economic chain of reasoning but asserted without quantification or evidence.

rigor.statement: The latest study shows early signs that our changes are working. Writing results for Year 6 students are up 5 per cent, and math results are up 6 per cent, helping to turn around New Zealand's long‑term drop in achievement between Years 4 and 8.
rigor.explanation: Offers figures but infers causation from correlation over a short period; the 'early signs' hedge is appropriate.

rigor.statement: By getting the books in order, cutting waste and keeping taxes low, we're able to keep investing in hospitals and services that matter to people.
rigor.explanation: Asserts a causal chain from fiscal restraint to service investment without evidence for the link.

authenticity.statement: The earlier return to surplus forecast in this year's Budget shows the benefits of disciplined economic management and a government taking its responsibilities seriously
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with National's stated fiscal-discipline brand, but the words-vs-record link cannot be verified from the text alone.

divination.statement: The growing economy is expected to create 220,000 more jobs over the next four years, with wages outstripping inflation over that period.
divination.explanation: Four-year forecast of job creation and real-wage growth; optimistic and dependent on volatile global conditions the release itself flags.

divination.statement: Without a responsible path back to surplus, Kiwis would face the real risk of higher debt, higher interest rates and higher taxes.
divination.explanation: Conditional prediction linking deficits to higher debt, rates and taxes; directionally defensible but stated as near-certain outcome.

civility.statement: Stalking causes serious emotional, psychological and economic harm, yet until now, stalkers have got away without facing serious legal consequences.
civility.explanation: Focuses on the problem and victims rather than attacking opponents.

specificity.statement: This budget delivers for Auckland families, businesses, and communities, and sends a strong signal of our commitment to supporting a thriving, resilient, globally competitive city,
specificity.explanation: Broad claim of 'delivering for Auckland' with no figures or mechanisms in this sentence.

specificity.statement: We're backing housing growth with a new $400 million fund that rewards councils that enable more homes, alongside planning and consenting reforms to make it easier and faster to build.
specificity.explanation: Names a $400m fund, its mechanism (rewarding councils that enable homes) and accompanying reforms.

specificity.statement: When Auckland succeeds, New Zealand succeeds.
specificity.explanation: Slogan with no concrete content.

strength.statement: We're backing housing growth with a new $400 million fund that rewards councils that enable more homes, alongside planning and consenting reforms to make it easier and faster to build.
strength.explanation: A concrete funded commitment, but announced in-Budget with delivery and uptake still ahead.

charisma.statement: This budget delivers for Auckland families, businesses, and communities, and sends a strong signal of our commitment to supporting a thriving, resilient, globally competitive city,
charisma.explanation: Upbeat and inclusive of multiple Auckland groups, but a one-sided promotional appeal.

charisma.statement: When Auckland succeeds, New Zealand succeeds.
charisma.explanation: A tidy unifying line linking city and nation, though a slogan rather than a persuasive argument.

veracity.statement: We've seen examples in the Far North, in Tauranga and in Hastings where individuals, such as iwi representatives and young people aged under 18, have been appointed to council committees and given voting rights without being elected by the community.
veracity.explanation: Cites specific councils and appointment types; broadly accurate that non-elected members have held committee voting rights, though framing selects contentious examples.

specificity.statement: Councillors are directly accountable to voters for their decisions. We are amending the Local Government Act 2002 so only elected members hold voting rights at council committee meetings,
specificity.explanation: Names the Act being amended and the precise change (voting rights limited to elected members).

specificity.statement: We've seen examples in the Far North, in Tauranga and in Hastings where individuals, such as iwi representatives and young people aged under 18, have been appointed to council committees and given voting rights without being elected by the community.
specificity.explanation: Names three specific councils and the categories of appointees involved.

specificity.statement: That's not democratic, so we're fixing it.
specificity.explanation: Asserts a fix without detail in this line (detail is elsewhere).

specificity.statement: Councils can still appoint non-elected members to offer professional advice and represent communities but those appointments will not come with voting rights or count towards a quorum.
specificity.explanation: Clearly delineates what appointed members can and cannot do (advise/represent, but no vote or quorum).

strength.statement: Councillors are directly accountable to voters for their decisions. We are amending the Local Government Act 2002 so only elected members hold voting rights at council committee meetings,
strength.explanation: Legislative change is underway via a bill before Parliament — beyond announcement but not yet enacted.

rigor.statement: Councillors are directly accountable to voters for their decisions. We are amending the Local Government Act 2002 so only elected members hold voting rights at council committee meetings,
rigor.explanation: Reasoning from a clear premise (elected = accountable) to the conclusion; coherent though it sidesteps trade-offs of excluding appointed expertise.

rigor.statement: That's not democratic, so we're fixing it.
rigor.explanation: A conclusory value-judgement ('not democratic') asserted rather than argued.

civility.statement: We've seen examples in the Far North, in Tauranga and in Hastings where individuals, such as iwi representatives and young people aged under 18, have been appointed to council committees and given voting rights without being elected by the community.
civility.explanation: Criticises a process rather than individuals, though singling out iwi representatives and under-18s could be read as pointed.

civility.statement: Councils can still appoint non-elected members to offer professional advice and represent communities but those appointments will not come with voting rights or count towards a quorum.
civility.explanation: Acknowledges the legitimate value of non-elected appointees while explaining the limit; measured and non-personal.

veracity.statement: New Zealand's declining gas reserves and tightening supply are creating significant problems and uncertainty for businesses and threatening wider economic impacts.
veracity.explanation: NZ natural gas reserves and production have genuinely been declining and tightening in recent years; directionally accurate, though 'threatening wider economic impacts' is somewhat speculative.

veracity.statement: For too long, the information that the Government and sector have had on gas reserves, production and demand has been fragmented, incomplete and outdated which is making the situation even harder to manage.
veracity.explanation: Plausible characterisation of fragmented gas-market data used to justify the bill, but self-serving and unverifiable from the text.

specificity.statement: New Zealand's declining gas reserves and tightening supply are creating significant problems and uncertainty for businesses and threatening wider economic impacts.
specificity.explanation: Identifies a concrete problem (declining reserves, tightening supply) but gives no figures, timeframe, or magnitude.

specificity.statement: This is part of the Government's focus on fixing the basics and building the future by strengthening New Zealand's energy security and supporting a more resilient economy.
specificity.explanation: Pure slogan ('fixing the basics and building the future') with no mechanism, figure, or measurable commitment.

specificity.statement: Instead, the Government is working on a number of practical measures simultaneously, including fast-tracking consents for more renewable electricity generation, and making the market fairer, to help ensure all New Zealand homes and businesses have access to an affordable and reliable energy supply.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete strands (fast-tracking renewable consents, market fairness) but no amounts, targets, or timeframes.

rigor.statement: New Zealand's declining gas reserves and tightening supply are creating significant problems and uncertainty for businesses and threatening wider economic impacts.
rigor.explanation: Reasonable causal claim linking supply decline to business uncertainty, but no evidence or data cited to support it.

rigor.statement: For too long, the information that the Government and sector have had on gas reserves, production and demand has been fragmented, incomplete and outdated which is making the situation even harder to manage.
rigor.explanation: States a problem-to-solution premise but relies on assertion ('fragmented, incomplete and outdated') without evidence.

rigor.statement: There is no single or quick solution to New Zealand's energy challenges.
rigor.explanation: A candid, defensible framing that avoids over-promising a silver bullet, though it is an assertion rather than an evidenced claim.

civility.statement: There is no single or quick solution to New Zealand's energy challenges.
civility.explanation: Measured, non-partisan, policy-focused acknowledgement of complexity.

strength.statement: Instead, the Government is working on a number of practical measures simultaneously, including fast-tracking consents for more renewable electricity generation, and making the market fairer, to help ensure all New Zealand homes and businesses have access to an affordable and reliable energy supply.
strength.explanation: Describes measures in progress; the transparency bill itself passed, but broader delivery on energy security is still unfolding.

veracity.statement: One in every seven people work in food and fibre – a successful sector means thriving communities, a growing economy and a prosperous New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: The 'one in seven' food-and-fibre employment figure is commonly cited and roughly in line with official estimates; the rest is aspirational framing.

specificity.statement: We are working hard alongside farmers and growers to achieve more with less,
specificity.explanation: Vague slogan; 'achieve more with less' commits to no mechanism or measure.

specificity.statement: Budget 2026 confirms $4.77 billion in baseline funding over the next four years year for the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) to support the primary sector and protect the frontline.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure ($4.77 billion), timeframe (four years), and named recipient (MPI).

specificity.statement: Its exports are set to top a record $62 billion this year.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figure ($62 billion) and timeframe (this year).

rigor.statement: One in every seven people work in food and fibre – a successful sector means thriving communities, a growing economy and a prosperous New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: Leans on the statistic to imply broad prosperity without demonstrating the causal chain.

strength.statement: Budget 2026 confirms $4.77 billion in baseline funding over the next four years year for the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) to support the primary sector and protect the frontline.
strength.explanation: A confirmed Budget appropriation, but it is baseline funding announced rather than an outcome delivered.

divination.statement: Its exports are set to top a record $62 billion this year.
divination.explanation: Forecast of record food-and-fibre exports for the year; plausible given strong export trends but not yet realised, timeframe within the year.

veracity.statement: Every year, the Ministry of Social Development (MSD) makes millions of decisions – many of them straightforward, but the legislation has not kept up with how services are delivered today.
veracity.explanation: MSD does make very large volumes of decisions annually; the claim that legislation lags service delivery is plausible and used to justify the bill.

specificity.statement: Every year, the Ministry of Social Development (MSD) makes millions of decisions – many of them straightforward, but the legislation has not kept up with how services are delivered today.
specificity.explanation: 'Millions of decisions' is broad; identifies the problem but no precise figures.

specificity.statement: Automated decision-making will be used where decisions are straightforward and do not require discretion. The system will not replace human judgement where it is appropriate, and in many cases will make it easier for people to confirm their circumstances.
specificity.explanation: Explains the scope of automation (straightforward, non-discretionary decisions) but no detail on which decision types or safeguards' mechanics.

specificity.statement: New Zealanders can have confidence that decisions will remain fair, accountable, and open to challenge.
specificity.explanation: General reassurance; no detail on how fairness or challenge rights are guaranteed beyond the assertion.

specificity.statement: This is about delegating straight-forward decision-making to an automated process, to free up time for case managers to engage better with clients so they can access assistance and move from welfare to work.
specificity.explanation: Articulates a clear intended mechanism (automate simple cases to free case-manager time) but no targets or measures of success.

civility.statement: Automated decision-making will be used where decisions are straightforward and do not require discretion. The system will not replace human judgement where it is appropriate, and in many cases will make it easier for people to confirm their circumstances.
civility.explanation: Measured, reassuring, policy-focused explanation with no partisan attack.

strength.statement: This is about delegating straight-forward decision-making to an automated process, to free up time for case managers to engage better with clients so they can access assistance and move from welfare to work.
strength.explanation: Tied to a bill that passed its third reading, but the welfare-to-work outcome is aspirational and not yet demonstrated.

veracity.statement: Strong UK consumer demand for our premium products has driven a 75 per cent increase in total New Zealand exports to this market in the three years of our Agreement,
veracity.explanation: A specific export-growth figure attributed to the NZ-UK FTA; plausible but the causal attribution solely to the FTA is a favourable framing.

veracity.statement: Last year alone, Kiwi goods exports to the UK rose over 22 per cent compared to 2024, with meat a key contributor to the growth. There was also a 28 per cent increase in business services exports.
veracity.explanation: Detailed, checkable trade statistics; consistent with reported post-FTA growth, presented accurately in tone though unverified here.

veracity.statement: One in four New Zealand jobs depends on trade, and strengthening these relationships creates opportunities for Kiwi businesses, meaning higher incomes and more jobs.
veracity.explanation: The 'one in four jobs depends on trade' figure is a commonly cited estimate broadly in line with official analysis; the downstream 'higher incomes and more jobs' is assertion.

specificity.statement: Strong UK consumer demand for our premium products has driven a 75 per cent increase in total New Zealand exports to this market in the three years of our Agreement,
specificity.explanation: Precise figure (75 per cent) over a defined period (three years of the Agreement).

specificity.statement: Last year alone, Kiwi goods exports to the UK rose over 22 per cent compared to 2024, with meat a key contributor to the growth. There was also a 28 per cent increase in business services exports.
specificity.explanation: Multiple precise figures with year comparisons and sector breakdowns.

specificity.statement: One in four New Zealand jobs depends on trade, and strengthening these relationships creates opportunities for Kiwi businesses, meaning higher incomes and more jobs.
specificity.explanation: One concrete ratio, but the promised benefits are stated without figures or timeframe.

rigor.statement: One in four New Zealand jobs depends on trade, and strengthening these relationships creates opportunities for Kiwi businesses, meaning higher incomes and more jobs.
rigor.explanation: Uses a real statistic but jumps to income/jobs benefits without demonstrating the causal link.

veracity.statement: But under Labour's CCCFA changes, lending became harder, slower, and more frustrating than it needed to be. Borrowers were put through intrusive and unnecessary checks, lenders became overly cautious, and good Kiwis were left jumping through hoops just to get a loan.
veracity.explanation: The 2021 CCCFA changes were widely reported to have tightened and slowed lending, so directionally supported, but 'intrusive and unnecessary' is a partisan characterisation.

specificity.statement: This Government promised to bring common sense back to lending, and today we have delivered.
specificity.explanation: 'Common sense back to lending' is a slogan; specificity comes only from the surrounding detail, not this sentence.

specificity.statement: We are also removing unnecessary personal liability for senior managers and directors and making consequences for certain disclosure breaches more proportionate. Accountability remains, but the rules need to be workable and fair.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete changes (removing personal liability, proportionate disclosure consequences) though without detail on thresholds.

specificity.statement: We have turned the page on Labour's bad CCCFA settings and delivered clearer rules, stronger competition, better access to finance, and proportionate consumer protection.
specificity.explanation: Lists claimed outcomes but without metrics for competition or access.

rigor.statement: But under Labour's CCCFA changes, lending became harder, slower, and more frustrating than it needed to be. Borrowers were put through intrusive and unnecessary checks, lenders became overly cautious, and good Kiwis were left jumping through hoops just to get a loan.
rigor.explanation: Plausible critique but relies on characterisation ('jumping through hoops') rather than cited evidence.

civility.statement: But under Labour's CCCFA changes, lending became harder, slower, and more frustrating than it needed to be. Borrowers were put through intrusive and unnecessary checks, lenders became overly cautious, and good Kiwis were left jumping through hoops just to get a loan.
civility.explanation: Harsh but largely policy-focused criticism of the previous government's rules; partisan framing ('Labour's') but not a personal attack.

civility.statement: We are also removing unnecessary personal liability for senior managers and directors and making consequences for certain disclosure breaches more proportionate. Accountability remains, but the rules need to be workable and fair.
civility.explanation: Substantive, balanced policy explanation acknowledging that accountability remains.

civility.statement: We have turned the page on Labour's bad CCCFA settings and delivered clearer rules, stronger competition, better access to finance, and proportionate consumer protection.
civility.explanation: Partisan 'Labour's bad settings' framing, but the criticism targets policy rather than individuals.

strength.statement: This Government promised to bring common sense back to lending, and today we have delivered.
strength.explanation: A stated commitment backed by enacted legislation (third reading passed), though the promised consumer benefits are yet to materialise.

strength.statement: We have turned the page on Labour's bad CCCFA settings and delivered clearer rules, stronger competition, better access to finance, and proportionate consumer protection.
strength.explanation: Claims delivery on enacted legislation, though 'stronger competition' and 'better access' are outcomes not yet demonstrated.

authenticity.statement: This Government promised to bring common sense back to lending, and today we have delivered.
authenticity.explanation: Claims delivery on a prior commitment to reform lending rules, consistent with the bill actually passing its third reading.

specificity.statement: Last week we announced a 20-year extension to copyright protection, keeping some of our most iconic works earning for the artists who created them.
specificity.explanation: Concrete measure (20-year copyright extension) with clear rationale.

specificity.statement: We are updating the Copyright Act so not-for-profit galleries, libraries, archives and museums have greater flexibility to make digital copies of works to help preserve them before they're lost and to open them up to public access.
specificity.explanation: Names the Act, the beneficiaries, and the concrete change (digital preservation copying) but no timeline or thresholds.

specificity.statement: We're also hitting back at offshore piracy. The courts will get a clear framework to block overseas websites that rip off the work of creators.
specificity.explanation: Identifies a concrete mechanism (court framework to block infringing overseas sites) but no detail on the framework.

specificity.statement: Looking ahead, Cabinet has invited me to report back by 31 March 2027 on a possible copyright framework for generative AI in New Zealand. Issues around AI and copyright are complex, and different countries have taken various approaches.
specificity.explanation: Concrete deliverable and date (report back by 31 March 2027) on a defined topic.

rigor.statement: Looking ahead, Cabinet has invited me to report back by 31 March 2027 on a possible copyright framework for generative AI in New Zealand. Issues around AI and copyright are complex, and different countries have taken various approaches.
rigor.explanation: Candidly acknowledges complexity and cross-country variation rather than overclaiming a settled answer.

civility.statement: We're also hitting back at offshore piracy. The courts will get a clear framework to block overseas websites that rip off the work of creators.
civility.explanation: Policy-focused; 'rip off' is colourful but aimed at pirate sites, not political opponents.

strength.statement: Last week we announced a 20-year extension to copyright protection, keeping some of our most iconic works earning for the artists who created them.
strength.explanation: An announced extension; delivery depends on legislation not yet described as enacted here.

forthrightness.statement: Looking ahead, Cabinet has invited me to report back by 31 March 2027 on a possible copyright framework for generative AI in New Zealand. Issues around AI and copyright are complex, and different countries have taken various approaches.
forthrightness.explanation: Openly notes the AI-copyright question is unresolved and being deferred to a future report rather than asserting a position.

veracity.statement: Budget 2026 invests an additional $69 million to double the number of trades academy places from 10,000 to 20,000.
veracity.explanation: Specific, internally consistent Budget figures presented as fact; plausible and checkable.

specificity.statement: This Government backs the trades. We know that for many young people, vocational education provides a direct pathway into skilled careers and lifelong opportunities,
specificity.explanation: Value statement / slogan ('backs the trades') with no mechanism or figure in this sentence.

specificity.statement: Budget 2026 invests an additional $69 million to double the number of trades academy places from 10,000 to 20,000.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure ($69 million) and concrete target (double places from 10,000 to 20,000).

specificity.statement: This investment means thousands more students will be able to access hands-on learning, gain industry experience, and develop the skills and knowledge they need for apprenticeships, further training, and employment while they are still at school,
specificity.explanation: 'Thousands more students' follows from the doubling but this sentence gives no independent figures.

specificity.statement: Alongside the expansion of trades academy places, the Government is investing a further $15 million for Industry Skills Boards (ISBs) to develop new vocational subjects as part of New Zealand's new senior secondary qualifications.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure ($15 million), named recipient (ISBs), and defined purpose (new vocational subjects).

specificity.statement: This Government rejects the idea that there is only one pathway to success.
specificity.explanation: Value statement with no concrete mechanism.

specificity.statement: Our new qualifications will give vocational pathways the same status, rigour, and recognition as any other pathway, giving young people more opportunities to succeed in the pathway that is right for them.
specificity.explanation: States an aim (equal status) but no measurable definition of how parity would be achieved or judged.

strength.statement: Budget 2026 invests an additional $69 million to double the number of trades academy places from 10,000 to 20,000.
strength.explanation: A funded Budget commitment; the doubling is an announced investment, delivery of the places will follow.

strength.statement: Alongside the expansion of trades academy places, the Government is investing a further $15 million for Industry Skills Boards (ISBs) to develop new vocational subjects as part of New Zealand's new senior secondary qualifications.
strength.explanation: Funded investment announced; the new subjects are still under development, so delivery is in progress.

divination.statement: This investment means thousands more students will be able to access hands-on learning, gain industry experience, and develop the skills and knowledge they need for apprenticeships, further training, and employment while they are still at school,
divination.explanation: Forecasts thousands more students gaining access; plausible given the funded doubling of places, though realisation depends on uptake.

divination.statement: Our new qualifications will give vocational pathways the same status, rigour, and recognition as any other pathway, giving young people more opportunities to succeed in the pathway that is right for them.
divination.explanation: Predicts parity of status for vocational pathways; aspirational and hard to verify, outcome depends on implementation and social perception.

charisma.statement: This Government rejects the idea that there is only one pathway to success.
charisma.explanation: An inclusive framing that seeks to validate multiple paths, but rhetorical and appeals mainly to supporters of vocational education.

specificity.statement: This initiative aims to improve outcomes for children and young people and contributes to the Government's target of reducing youth offending by 2030.
specificity.explanation: References a dated target (reducing youth offending by 2030) but this programme's contribution is unquantified.

specificity.statement: We are investing in trusted community organisations with proven capability and strong local connections to support children and young people through the positive vehicle of physical activity and sport,
specificity.explanation: Describes the approach (funding proven community organisations via sport) but names no organisations or amounts in this sentence.

specificity.statement: The first wave has been approved that will see $2.2 million support five organisations.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure ($2.2 million) and count (five organisations) for an approved first wave.

rigor.statement: I have seen firsthand the difference that sport and recreation can make in the lives of young people.
rigor.explanation: Personal-anecdote appeal ('seen firsthand') offered as justification rather than evidence of programme effectiveness.

strength.statement: This initiative aims to improve outcomes for children and young people and contributes to the Government's target of reducing youth offending by 2030.
strength.explanation: Links funding to a stated target; delivery on the 2030 goal is unproven and this is one contributing initiative.

strength.statement: The first wave has been approved that will see $2.2 million support five organisations.
strength.explanation: A concrete, approved allocation—actual delivery beyond approval still to follow.

authenticity.statement: I have seen firsthand the difference that sport and recreation can make in the lives of young people.
authenticity.explanation: A stated personal conviction consistent with his sport/recreation portfolio; no contradiction visible, but not independently verifiable.

veracity.statement: It enables a move away from the burdensome process of assembling individual Evidence Portfolios that was required under the PBRF.
veracity.explanation: Accurate that the PBRF required individual Evidence Portfolios; 'burdensome' is a fair but subjective characterisation.

specificity.statement: The new fund will significantly reduce compliance costs for tertiary education organisations
specificity.explanation: Claims cost reduction but gives no figure or baseline for 'significantly'.

specificity.statement: It enables a move away from the burdensome process of assembling individual Evidence Portfolios that was required under the PBRF.
specificity.explanation: Names the concrete change (removing Evidence Portfolios) that was a well-known feature of the PBRF.

specificity.statement: It also includes a greater focus on impact – through external research income and new metrics for citations, commercialisation and policy outcomes.
specificity.explanation: Lists concrete new metrics (external research income, citations, commercialisation, policy outcomes) for the fund's design.

specificity.statement: The TREF will support New Zealand's future skills and innovation needs by rewarding research excellence and impact in a more responsive and efficient way.
specificity.explanation: General statement of purpose; 'more responsive and efficient' lacks a measurable definition.

divination.statement: The new fund will significantly reduce compliance costs for tertiary education organisations
divination.explanation: Predicts a significant reduction in compliance costs from replacing PBRF; plausible given removal of Evidence Portfolios but 'significantly' is unquantified.

divination.statement: The TREF will support New Zealand's future skills and innovation needs by rewarding research excellence and impact in a more responsive and efficient way.
divination.explanation: Implicit forecast that the fund will meet future skills/innovation needs; too broad to verify precisely.

divination.statement: The economy is expected to grow, on average, by 2.7% each year over the next four years.
divination.explanation: Four-year forecast of 2.7% average annual growth; plausible and broadly in line with Treasury forecasting but medium-term growth is uncertain.

divination.statement: Despite global turmoil, New Zealand will also return to surplus in 2028/29 (one year faster than forecast), and thankfully our borrowing will be reduced by $6 billion.
divination.explanation: Predicts a 2028/29 surplus; NZ surplus forecasts have repeatedly slipped, so a firm return-to-surplus date carries real downside risk.

divination.statement: This will result in $2.4 billion of savings over four years which will be redirected into frontline services.
divination.explanation: Projects savings from public-sector cuts; forecast savings of this kind often fall short of target, so uncertain.

specificity.statement: The economy is expected to grow, on average, by 2.7% each year over the next four years.
specificity.explanation: Names a precise figure (2.7%) and timeframe (four years).

specificity.statement: Despite global turmoil, New Zealand will also return to surplus in 2028/29 (one year faster than forecast), and thankfully our borrowing will be reduced by $6 billion.
specificity.explanation: Gives a fiscal year (2028/29) and a dollar figure ($6 billion) for reduced borrowing.

specificity.statement: By stopping wasteful spending, finding savings and making careful choices, we are getting the books in order and keeping taxes low while continuing to invest in the frontline services and infrastructure that Kiwis care about.
specificity.explanation: Broad governing slogan; no figures, mechanisms or named measures.

specificity.statement: This will result in $2.4 billion of savings over four years which will be redirected into frontline services.
specificity.explanation: Concrete dollar figure ($2.4b) and timeframe (four years), though the redirection mechanism is unspecified.

specificity.statement: Budget 2026 doubles trade training opportunities, with the number of Trades Academy places increasing from 10,000 to 20,000.
specificity.explanation: Precise before/after figures (10,000 to 20,000).

specificity.statement: From midnight 27 May, stalking is a criminal offence punishable by up to five years in prison.
specificity.explanation: Names the date (27 May) and maximum penalty (five years).

specificity.statement: The watching, the following, the tracking that has ruined so many lives will now be a crime – before it turns deadly. We have fixed the law so you do not have to face the fear.
specificity.explanation: Emotive framing of the reform; gestures at conduct covered but no detail beyond the general offence.

rigor.statement: This is straight from the Labour playbook of scamming Kiwis with a glossy headline that sounds nice but will never be delivered. We saw it with light rail, and we saw it with KiwiBuild.

rigor.statement: If Labour can't get their numbers right on what the policy will cost, they certainly can't be trusted on their claims about how it will be paid for.

veracity.statement: Many New Zealanders would be surprised to know there are smaller penalties for some forms of deplorable human trafficking offences than others,

veracity.statement: As it stands, section 98D of the Crimes Act, which deals with trafficking in persons, allows for a penalty of imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of up to $500,000. Section 98, which covers dealing in slaves, also allows for 14-year penalties.

civility.statement: This bill will modernise New Zealand’s approach to human trafficking and ensure instances of domestic trafficking are treated as seriously as international. I look forward to building support across other parties in the House.

strength.statement: From September this year, the starting age for free bowel screening will be lowered from 58 to 56, extending access to hundreds of thousands more New Zealanders and continuing our commitment to align New Zealand’s screening age with Australia.

veracity.statement: The Official Cash Rate went from 0.25 per cent to 5.5 per cent and has remained there for a year.

veracity.explanation: Broadly accurate on both endpoints, though a large part of the rise reflects COVID-era spending she acknowledges elsewhere; the framing selects a favourable base year.

veracity.statement: Compared to the Half Year Update, the Budget Update expects core Crown tax revenue to be lower by around $18.5 billion across the forecast period as a result of lower GDP and lower business income tax.

veracity.statement: The final allowance in this year's Budget is in fact $3.2 billion. This is the lowest allowance in nominal terms since Budget 2018 and the lowest in real terms (that is, adjusting for inflation) since Budget 2017.
veracity.explanation: Specific and checkable; consistent with the operating-allowance record for the period.

veracity.statement: By comparison, the final operating allowances for the last two Labour Budgets were $5.9 billion in 2022 and $4.8 billion in 2023.
veracity.explanation: Broadly matches the reported final operating allowances for Budgets 2022 and 2023.

veracity.statement: Analysis from the Treasury shows that an estimated 727,000 households will benefit by at least $75 a fortnight, and 187,000 will benefit by at least $100 a fortnight. On average, households will benefit by $60 a fortnight, and households with children by $78 a fortnight.
veracity.explanation: Sourced to Treasury analysis with 'estimated'/'up to' hedging; the averages are technically accurate though favourable framing of a distribution.

veracity.explanation: The named measures are targeted, but characterising the whole package as not favouring higher earners is partly true and omits that threshold rises give larger dollar gains to higher incomes.

veracity.statement: Tax relief in this Budget puts $3.7 billion a year back into the pockets of New Zealanders.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with Budget costings for the package; the 'back into pockets' framing is favourable but the figure is defensible.

veracity.statement: This tax relief is fully funded. Some of the funding is from revenue measures, but mostly it comes from savings.
veracity.explanation: Defensible in that offsets were identified, though 'fully funded' amid rising debt and deficits is contestable framing.

veracity.statement: This scrutiny has resulted in more than 240 savings initiatives.
veracity.explanation: A concrete, verifiable count consistent with Budget 2024 documentation.

veracity.statement: This package of tax relief is identical in most respects to that set out in National's election tax plan. veracity.statement: New Zealand remains on track to reach the emission reduction goals of our first emission reduction period.

veracity.explanation: A contestable value-laden claim; the debt rise she cites was substantially COVID-driven, so 'mismanagement' overstates.

specificity.statement: The Government intends to get back to surplus in 2027/28.

divination.statement: The Government intends to get back to surplus in 2027/28.

authenticity.statement: Fortunately, the parties in this coalition Government are the parties of the worker.

authenticity.explanation: Delivers the tax plan campaigned on, and openly flags the one deviation (a ~4-week delay) with a stated reason — words matching deeds.

authenticity.statement: In particular, I engaged closely and constructively with my colleague David Seymour on the ACT Party's idea of flattening the tax scale. authenticity.explanation: Acknowledges testing an alternative and explains why it was set aside, consistent with a transparent process.

civility.statement: By comparison, the final operating allowances for the last two Labour Budgets were $5.9 billion in 2022 and $4.8 billion in 2023.

civility.explanation: Sharp, incredulous criticism of the previous government but aimed at a funding decision and figures, not personal character.

civility.statement: This year's Budget is the clean-up job New Zealand needs after six years of economic mismanagement.

civility.statement: I want to acknowledge and thank the Associate Ministers of Finance – David Seymour, Shane Jones and Chris Bishop – who were heavily involved in putting this Budget together.

charisma.statement: We will be making difficult decisions and trade-offs to turn the fiscal situation around, get back to surplus and reduce debt, because that is what is required. But New Zealanders should know this – we will look after them along the way.

charisma.statement: Fortunately, the parties in this coalition Government are the parties of the worker.

veracity.statement: New Zealand's Exclusive Economic Zone covers four million square kilometres of ocean. Less than one per cent of that could generate 600 per cent of this country's electricity needs from renewable energy.
veracity.explanation: The four-million-sq-km EEZ figure is broadly accurate; the '600 per cent' generation claim is a theoretical potential estimate, plausible but not independently verifiable from the text.

veracity.explanation: It is true offshore wind is well established overseas and NZ lacked a settled regulatory regime; attributing the entire gap to Labour inaction over six years is a partisan simplification.

specificity.statement: New Zealand's Exclusive Economic Zone covers four million square kilometres of ocean. Less than one per cent of that could generate 600 per cent of this country's electricity needs from renewable energy.

strength.statement: Today, I am proud to announce that National will fast track rules to unleash investment in offshore wind generation as part of our plan to Electrify NZ.

strength.statement: I will be working across the house to gather the support necessary to have this passed into law.

veracity.statement: Our record health investment is already delivering results, with more elective surgeries being completed, higher childhood immunisation rates, and shorter waits in emergency departments.
veracity.explanation: Some targeted metrics improved, but health-system performance data was mixed; presenting selected gains as proof of delivery omits contrary indicators.

specificity.statement: We are focused on improving access to healthcare, reducing wait times, strengthening frontline health services, and delivering against our health targets, so New Zealanders can get the care they need, when they need it.
specificity.explanation: Lists focus areas as themes without figures, timeframes, or mechanisms.

strength.statement: Our record health investment is already delivering results, with more elective surgeries being completed, higher childhood immunisation rates, and shorter waits in emergency departments.
strength.explanation: Claims credit for delivered outcomes tied to health targets, with partial supporting evidence.

veracity.statement: On 31 July this year, New Zealanders will experience tax relief for the first time in 14 years.

veracity.statement: A single person earning $55,000 a year will be better off by about $51 a fortnight.

veracity.statement: The changes will be fully paid for with off-setting savings and revenue initiatives, meaning tax relief won't require additional borrowing and won't add to inflation pressure.
veracity.explanation: The package was structured as fiscally neutral via savings and revenue, though the claim of zero inflation impact is a contested economic judgement.

specificity.statement: On 31 July this year, New Zealanders will experience tax relief for the first time in 14 years.
specificity.explanation: Gives an exact commencement date.

specificity.statement: A single person earning $55,000 a year will be better off by about $51 a fortnight.
specificity.explanation: Precise income level and dollar benefit.

charisma.statement: As agreed in the National-Act agreement, I engaged closely and constructively with ACT leader David Seymour on the idea of flattening the tax scale. This has a lot of merit but was not possible to achieve in a way that benefitted people as the National plan did. It remains, however, an idea for the future.

authenticity.statement: Our Government was elected to give a fairer deal to hardworking New Zealanders and the tax package we are confirming today delivers on that promise.

forthrightness.statement: As agreed in the National-Act agreement, I engaged closely and constructively with ACT leader David Seymour on the idea of flattening the tax scale. forthrightness.explanation: Candidly explains why a partner's proposal was not adopted while leaving the door open.

veracity.statement: High inflation and high interest rates pummelled families, and the wider economy leading to the biggest recession since 1991.
veracity.explanation: NZ did enter recession in 2024, but calling it 'the biggest recession since 1991' overstates it — the 2020 COVID contraction and the 2008-09 GFC were larger by standard GDP measures, so the superlative is misleading.

veracity.statement: Wages are growing faster than inflation, food prices are rising slowly, and cost pressures – like the Auckland Regional Fuel Tax – have been sucked out of the economy.
veracity.explanation: By late 2024 wage growth did outpace CPI, food-price inflation had eased, and the Auckland Regional Fuel Tax was abolished on 30 June 2024 — all broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: For anyone with a mortgage, that means real savings – around $200 per fortnight for someone looking to re-fix a $500,000 mortgage.
veracity.explanation: Plausible for the rate drops of late 2024, but the ~$200/fortnight depends on assumed rate movements not stated, so it is only conditionally accurate.

veracity.statement: And just as we campaigned on, the tax relief we delivered last year means Kiwis are keeping more of what they earn, for the first time in fourteen years.
veracity.explanation: Income-tax thresholds had been unchanged since 2010, so 'first time in fourteen years' is roughly right, though thresholds not wages is the precise referent.

veracity.statement: We are getting kids out of emergency housing – more than 1,700 children out of motels and into homes so far under our government.
veracity.explanation: Emergency-housing motel numbers did fall sharply through 2024; the ~1,700 children figure aligns with reported government data, though methodology on where they went is contested.

veracity.statement: We are making major investments in health – to the tune of $17 billion in last year’s Budget.
veracity.explanation: Budget 2024 health funding of ~$16.7b was a multi-year total; presenting it as a single figure omits that context and slightly rounds up.

veracity.statement: Last year the OECD said that insufficient competition was an important factor in driving New Zealand’s long standing productivity woes.
veracity.explanation: The OECD has repeatedly flagged weak domestic competition and productivity in its NZ analysis, so the attribution is broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: I wouldn’t be shocked if cones were New Zealand’s fastest growing industry. They’re everywhere.
veracity.explanation: Deliberate exaggeration not intended as literal fact.

veracity.statement: In Denmark – a country like New Zealand of around five million people – recent pharmaceutical breakthroughs have delivered a modern economic miracle – creating a tidal wave of growth, employment, and opportunity.
veracity.explanation: Denmark's Novo Nordisk-led boom is real, but its population is ~5.9m (rounded down to 'around five million') and 'tidal wave/economic miracle' is hyperbolic.

veracity.statement: We’re cracking down on gangs and restoring order in our towns and cities, with more foot patrols and more visible policing.
veracity.explanation: Legislative measures were enacted, though 'restoring order' as an achieved outcome is asserted rather than demonstrated.

veracity.statement: Interest rates are falling and the Reserve Bank is forecasting more relief on the way soon.
veracity.explanation: Accurate as at January 2025 — the RBNZ had begun cutting the OCR in late 2024 and signalled further cuts.

veracity.statement: Whether it’s our record investment in health, ensuring so many Kiwis who waited so long for new cancer drugs, are now receiving treatment.
veracity.explanation: Pharmac's expanded medicines budget did fund new cancer drugs, though 'record investment' framing omits that the funding partly restored a shortfall.

specificity.statement: High inflation and high interest rates pummelled families, and the wider economy leading to the biggest recession since 1991.
specificity.explanation: Anchors the claim to a datable benchmark ('since 1991') but gives no figures for the size of the recession.

specificity.statement: Wages are growing faster than inflation, food prices are rising slowly, and cost pressures – like the Auckland Regional Fuel Tax – have been sucked out of the economy.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete effects and a specific policy (the fuel tax) but attaches no numbers to the wage or price movements.

specificity.statement: For anyone with a mortgage, that means real savings – around $200 per fortnight for someone looking to re-fix a $500,000 mortgage.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar figure, a period, and an illustrative loan size.

specificity.statement: We are getting kids out of emergency housing – more than 1,700 children out of motels and into homes so far under our government.
specificity.explanation: Concrete count of children and a defined outcome.

specificity.statement: We are making major investments in health – to the tune of $17 billion in last year’s Budget.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar figure and the source (last year's Budget).

specificity.statement: At a minimum, my expectation is we introduce legislation to Parliament this year to do exactly that.
specificity.explanation: Commits to a house (introducing RMA-replacement legislation) within a stated timeframe (this year), but hedged as an 'expectation'.

specificity.statement: Our political opponents can continue the scare campaigns of the early 2000s. But, we will back the scientific community, push on, and get that law passed this year too.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete goal (passing the law this year) but no detail on the legislation's content.

specificity.statement: I can announce today we have agreed to establish Invest New Zealand as the Government’s one-stop-shop for attracting foreign direct investment.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific new agency and its purpose, though not its budget, staffing, or start date.

specificity.statement: First, Cabinet has agreed to shake up our Crown Research Institutes, establishing four Public Research Organisations – focused on bio-economy, earth sciences, health and forensic sciences, and advanced technology.
specificity.explanation: Precise: a defined number of new bodies and their four named focus areas.

specificity.statement: We are powering up KiwiBank to take on the Aussie banks.
specificity.explanation: Names the entity and aim but no mechanism, capital figure, or timeframe.

charisma.statement: The public service exists to serve New Zealanders - not to be a breeding ground for identity politics.

specificity.statement: This is a rebuild project that has been waiting for 15 years now, and the time has come to ensure this vitally iconic symbol of Christchurch City is completed
specificity.explanation: Gives a timeframe and identifies the project but no delivery mechanism in this sentence.

specificity.explanation: Backed elsewhere in the release by a stated $15m figure, but this line itself is a general commitment to fund.

veracity.statement: This is a rebuild project that has been waiting for 15 years now, and the time has come to ensure this vitally iconic symbol of Christchurch City is completed
veracity.explanation: The cathedral has been damaged and stalled since the 2011 earthquake, so "waiting for 15 years" (to 2026) is broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: When last in government in 2018 we ensured a government commitment of $25 million towards the project, made up of $10 million with an additional $15 million interest free loan.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with the record: the 2018 coalition government committed a $10m grant plus a $15m interest-free loan to the cathedral reinstatement.

authenticity.statement: When last in government in 2018 we ensured a government commitment of $25 million towards the project, made up of $10 million with an additional $15 million interest free loan.

strength.statement: When last in government in 2018 we ensured a government commitment of $25 million towards the project, made up of $10 million with an additional $15 million interest free loan.

specificity.explanation: Platitude-level language ("practical solutions to improve quality of life") with no mechanism or figures.

veracity.statement: This week, for the first time in 14 years, New Zealanders got tax relief.

veracity.statement: We've delivered for working people, with an average income household better off by around $102 per fortnight
veracity.explanation: The $102 figure applied to a specific household type (with children, claiming FamilyBoost/childcare rebates), not a typical 'average income household'; presenting it as the average is misleading.

veracity.statement: We've delivered for full-time minimum wage workers, who instead of paying 30 cents of tax in the dollar for extra hours worked will now pay 17.5 cents in that dollar.
veracity.explanation: Threshold shift did move some income from the 30% to the 17.5% bracket; broadly accurate though it applies only to the portion of income crossing the changed threshold.

veracity.statement: families with children, who on top of their tax reduction will get back a Family Boost payment of up to $150 per fortnight to help pay their early childhood education fees.
veracity.explanation: FamilyBoost's advertised maximum of $150 per fortnight is accurate; 'up to' correctly signals it is a cap not a typical amount.

veracity.statement: we've put a stop to the war on landlords, bringing the brightline test back to two years and treating the interest costs of rental properties the same way as for every other business.
veracity.explanation: Brightline reduction to two years and reinstated interest deductibility are accurate; 'same way as every other business' glosses over property-specific rules.

veracity.statement: Labour had six years to lower tax and they never never did.
veracity.explanation: Labour did not cut income tax rates/thresholds 2017-2023, so directionally true, but it introduced other tax measures and a new top rate, so 'never lowered tax' is a simplification.

veracity.statement: In opposition, they have voted against every measure of tax relief we've introduced.

veracity.explanation: Consistent with Budget 2024 savings/reprioritisation figures, though 'savings' bundles reprioritisation and new revenue, which softens the claim.

veracity.statement: Over its time in office, Labour more than doubled New Zealand's net debt as a proportion of the economy, from less than 20 per cent of GDP to more than 40 per cent.
veracity.explanation: Net core Crown debt did roughly double as a share of GDP over 2017-2023, spanning the COVID period; accurate on the numbers though it omits the pandemic context driving it.

veracity.statement: In dollar terms, that is a whopping $120 billion of additional debt. To put it in perspective, that's around $24,000 in extra public debt for every single New Zealander.
veracity.explanation: The dollar and per-capita figures are broadly in the right range; 'whopping' adds rhetorical colour and the framing omits the COVID cause of the increase.

veracity.statement: This time a year ago it was an eye-watering 6 per cent, today it's 3.3 per cent, on track to come back under 3 per cent this year.
veracity.explanation: CPI inflation was 6.0% in the year to June 2023 and 3.3% to June 2024 — the figures are accurate.
